    +struct InterruptReader<Input> {
    +    input: Input,
    +    interrupt: bool,
    +}
    +
    +impl<Input: Read> Read for InterruptReader<Input> {
    +    fn read(&mut self, buffer: &mut [u8]) -> io::Result<usize> {
    +        if self.interrupt {
    +            self.interrupt = false;
    +            return Err(io::ErrorKind::Interrupted.into());
    +        }
    +        self.interrupt = true;
    +        self.input.read(buffer)
    +    }
    +}
    +
    +#[test]
    +fn read_interrupts_do_not_discard_partial_transactions() {
    +    let input = InterruptReader {
    +        input: ShortStream {
    +            inner: b"type,client,txid,amount\ndeposit,1,1,1.0001\n".as_slice(),
    +            limit: 3,
    +        },
    +        interrupt: true,

    # legendary-octo-spork
    
    Process account transactions from CSV with exact integer arithmetic and four decimal places.
    
    ```sh
    cargo run --release -- input.csv > accounts.csv
    ```
    
    The CLI accepts exactly one file path. It writes account CSV to stdout and transaction errors to stderr. Invalid CSV or an I/O failure produces a nonzero exit status. The processor reads the complete input before it writes account output.
    
    Input requires the columns `type,client,txid,amount` exactly once, in any order. The parser trims surrounding whitespace. Every row must contain four fields; control records can leave `amount` empty.
    
    ```csv
    type,client,txid,amount
    deposit,1,1,2.0001
    withdrawal,1,2,0.5000
    dispute,1,1,
    resolve,1,1,
    deposit,2,3,1
    ```
    
    This input produces:
    
    ```csv
    client,available,held,total,locked
    1,1.5001,0.0000,1.5001,false
    2,1.0000,0.0000,1.0000,false
    ```
    
    Output uses ascending client IDs and exactly four decimal places. Client IDs use `u16`; transaction IDs use `u32`. Both types accept zero. Amount syntax requires integer digits and optionally a decimal point with one to four fractional digits. The processor rejects excess precision, exponent notation, and amounts outside the numeric range. It never rounds or converts amounts through floating point.
    
    | Operation | Requirements | Account changes |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | Deposit | New transaction ID; nonnegative amount | Increase total and available |
    | Withdrawal | New transaction ID; nonnegative amount; sufficient available funds | Decrease total and available |
    | Dispute | The same client's deposit without an active dispute | Increase funds on hold; decrease available |
    | Resolve | The same client's deposit with an active dispute | Decrease funds on hold; increase available |
    | Chargeback | The same client's deposit with an active dispute | Decrease total and funds on hold; lock the account |
    
    A resolve permits another dispute on the same deposit. Withdrawals do not support dispute, resolve, or chargeback. Disputes can make available funds negative after a withdrawal. A chargeback can make total funds negative and prevents all later activity on the account, including changes to other disputes.
    
    Transaction IDs have global scope. The engine rejects duplicate deposits and withdrawals, references to another client's transaction, invalid state changes, negative amounts, and arithmetic overflow. These errors leave balances and transaction status unchanged; the processor reports each error and continues. Only successful deposits and withdrawals reserve new transaction IDs. The first monetary operation with a new transaction ID and a nonnegative amount creates a client account, including a withdrawal with insufficient funds. Invalid control records do not create accounts. Control records always use the deposit amount; a nonempty amount field still requires valid decimal syntax.
    
    The library separates transaction processing from CSV and stream access:
    
    | API | Use |
    | --- | --- |
    | `process_csv(input, output, diagnostics)` | CSV pipeline over any `Read` input and `Write` outputs, using `i64` amounts |
    | `CsvTransactions::<_, Value>::new(input)` | Fallible transaction iterator over any `Read` input; reuse one CSV byte record |
    | `process_txs(transactions, diagnostics)` | Consume any iterator of `Result<Transaction<Value>, Error>` and return the account map |
    | `Engine::<Value>::default()` and `apply(transaction)` | Process records incrementally while preserving account and transaction state |
    | `write_clients(&clients, output)` | Serialize an account map to any `Write` output |
    
    For memory streams:
    
    ```rust
    use legendary_octo_spork::process_csv;
    
    let input = b"type,client,txid,amount\ndeposit,1,1,1.2345\n";
    let mut output = Vec::new();
    let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
    process_csv(input.as_slice(), &mut output, &mut diagnostics)?;
    ```
    
    For a blocking TCP connection:
    
    ```rust
    use std::error::Error;
    use std::net::TcpStream;
    use legendary_octo_spork::process_csv;
    
    fn process_connection(mut stream: TcpStream) -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> {
        let input = stream.try_clone()?;
        process_csv(input, &mut stream, std::io::stderr().lock())?;
        Ok(())
    }
    ```
    
    The peer must finish its input, for example with `shutdown(Shutdown::Write)`, before reading the account response. The integration suite checks this exchange over a real loopback TCP connection. For connections without an end of input, feed records to `Engine::apply` and use `write_clients` when the application requires a snapshot. These APIs use blocking I/O.
    
    `Money<Value>` stores minor units, so `Money(12_345_i64)` represents `1.2345`. `MoneyValue` supplies checked integer operations. The library implements it for `i64` and `i128`; use `i128` for larger amounts while supporting negative balances. `CsvTransactions::<_, i128>`, `process_txs`, and `write_clients` support that type without changes to decimal parsing. `ClientId`, `TxId`, and `Money` implement `Deref`. Transaction variants require an amount for deposits and withdrawals, and account fields remain private so callers cannot bypass balance checks.
    
    The processor does not collect input records. It reuses CSV record storage and uses 64 KiB buffers for input, output, and diagnostics. The reader retries interrupted reads before CSV parsing. Processing takes expected linear time in the number of records, plus account sorting. Memory grows with client count, unique successful monetary transactions, and the largest CSV record. The engine retains transaction history for duplicate detection, later disputes, and withdrawal validation. Repeated dispute and resolve operations reuse an existing history entry.
    
    Run checks and the throughput benchmark with:
    
    ```sh
    cargo test --locked
    cargo test --release --locked
    cargo fmt --all -- --check
    cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
    cargo bench --bench throughput --locked
    ```
    
    The benchmark generates input before timing, performs one warmup, and reports the median of five runs. Every run checks all account rows and requires an empty diagnostic stream. It covers one million unique deposits and about one million mixed records, including all five transaction types. Adjust its size with `TX_BENCH_ROWS` and its repetitions with `TX_BENCH_ROUNDS`.
    
    On 2026-10-17, Rust 1.94.1 on an Intel Core i9-13900K in this Linux container produced:
    
    | In-memory CSV workload | Records | Median time | Records/second | Input MiB/second |
    | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
    | Unique deposits, 1,024 clients | 1,000,000 | 0.190 s | 5.27 million | 129.59 |
    | Deposits, withdrawals, disputes, resolves, and chargebacks | 1,002,048 | 0.150 s | 6.69 million | 149.46 |
    
    Separate CLI measurements use files with one million and four million rows, with three runs per input and complete output validation. Linux `VmHWM` samples track peak process memory after startup:
    
    | CLI workload | Records | Median time | Records/second | Peak memory |
    | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
    | Unique deposits, 1,024 clients | 1,000,000 | 0.200 s | 4.99 million | 101.3 MiB |
    | Unique deposits, 1,024 clients | 4,000,000 | 0.807 s | 4.96 million | 398.2 MiB |
    | Repeated dispute/resolve on one deposit | 1,000,000 | 0.115 s | 8.73 million | 2.3 MiB |
    | Repeated dispute/resolve on one deposit | 4,000,000 | 0.420 s | 9.53 million | 2.2 MiB |
    
    These measurements describe this environment; the benchmark does not enforce a hardware-dependent timing limit. History growth accounts for the memory increase with unique deposits. Repeated control records do not increase history size.
    use std::fmt;
    use std::marker::PhantomData;
    use std::ops::{Deref, Div, Rem};
    use std::str::FromStr;
    
    use serde::de::{self, Visitor};
    use serde::{Deserialize, Deserializer, Serialize, Serializer};
    
    pub const MONEY_PRECISION: u32 = 4;
    pub const MONEY_SCALE: u16 = 10_u16.pow(MONEY_PRECISION);
    
    pub trait MoneyValue:
        Copy + Ord + fmt::Debug + fmt::Display + From<u16> + Div<Output = Self> + Rem<Output = Self>
    {
        const ZERO: Self;
    
        fn checked_add(self, other: Self) -> Option<Self>;
        fn checked_sub(self, other: Self) -> Option<Self>;
        fn checked_mul(self, other: Self) -> Option<Self>;
    }
    
    macro_rules! impl_money_value {
        ($($value_type:ty),+ $(,)?) => {
            $(
                impl MoneyValue for $value_type {
                    const ZERO: Self = 0;
    
                    fn checked_add(self, other: Self) -> Option<Self> {
                        self.checked_add(other)
                    }
    
                    fn checked_sub(self, other: Self) -> Option<Self> {
                        self.checked_sub(other)
                    }
    
                    fn checked_mul(self, other: Self) -> Option<Self> {
                        self.checked_mul(other)
                    }
                }
            )+
        };
    }
    
    impl_money_value!(i64, i128);
    
    #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, Hash, Ord, PartialEq, PartialOrd)]
    #[repr(transparent)]
    pub struct Money<Value>(pub Value);
    
    impl<Value> Deref for Money<Value> {
        type Target = Value;
    
        fn deref(&self) -> &Self::Target {
            &self.0
        }
    }
    
    #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
    pub enum MoneyError {
        Syntax,
        Precision,
        Overflow,
    }
    
    impl fmt::Display for MoneyError {
        fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
            formatter.write_str(match self {
                Self::Syntax => "amount must contain decimal digits with an optional minus sign",
                Self::Precision => "amount exceeds four decimal places",
                Self::Overflow => "amount exceeds the numeric range",
            })
        }
    }
    
    impl std::error::Error for MoneyError {}
    
    impl<Value: MoneyValue> FromStr for Money<Value> {
        type Err = MoneyError;
    
        fn from_str(text: &str) -> Result<Self, Self::Err> {
            let (negative, digits) = match text.strip_prefix('-') {
                Some(digits) => (true, digits),
                None => (false, text),
            };
            let (whole, fraction) = match digits.split_once('.') {
                Some((whole, fraction)) if !fraction.is_empty() => (whole, fraction),
                Some(_) => return Err(MoneyError::Syntax),
                None => (digits, ""),
            };
            if whole.is_empty() {
                return Err(MoneyError::Syntax);
            }
            if fraction.len() > MONEY_PRECISION as usize {
                return Err(MoneyError::Precision);
            }
            let mut minor_units = Value::ZERO;
            let ten = Value::from(10);
            for digit in whole.bytes().chain(fraction.bytes()) {
                if !digit.is_ascii_digit() {
                    return Err(MoneyError::Syntax);
                }
                let digit_value = Value::from(u16::from(digit - b'0'));
                minor_units = minor_units
                    .checked_mul(ten)
                    .and_then(|value| {
                        if negative {
                            value.checked_sub(digit_value)
                        } else {
                            value.checked_add(digit_value)
                        }
                    })
                    .ok_or(MoneyError::Overflow)?;
            }
            for _ in fraction.len()..MONEY_PRECISION as usize {
                minor_units = minor_units.checked_mul(ten).ok_or(MoneyError::Overflow)?;
            }
            Ok(Self(minor_units))
        }
    }
    
    impl<Value: MoneyValue> fmt::Display for Money<Value> {
        fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
            let scale = Value::from(MONEY_SCALE);
            let mut whole = self.0 / scale;
            let mut fraction = self.0 % scale;
            if self.0 < Value::ZERO {
                formatter.write_str("-")?;
                whole = Value::ZERO.checked_sub(whole).ok_or(fmt::Error)?;
                fraction = Value::ZERO.checked_sub(fraction).ok_or(fmt::Error)?;
            }
            write!(
                formatter,
                "{whole}.{fraction:0width$}",
                width = MONEY_PRECISION as usize
            )
        }
    }
    
    impl<Value: MoneyValue> Serialize for Money<Value> {
        fn serialize<Output: Serializer>(
            &self,
            serializer: Output,
        ) -> Result<Output::Ok, Output::Error> {
            serializer.collect_str(self)
        }
    }
    
    struct MoneyVisitor<Value>(PhantomData<Value>);
    
    impl<'input, Value: MoneyValue> Visitor<'input> for MoneyVisitor<Value> {
        type Value = Money<Value>;
    
        fn expecting(&self, formatter: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
            formatter.write_str("a decimal amount with at most four decimal places")
        }
    
        fn visit_str<Error: de::Error>(self, value: &str) -> Result<Self::Value, Error> {
            value.parse().map_err(de::Error::custom)
        }
    }
    
    impl<'input, Value: MoneyValue> Deserialize<'input> for Money<Value> {
        fn deserialize<Input: Deserializer<'input>>(deserializer: Input) -> Result<Self, Input::Error> {
            deserializer.deserialize_str(MoneyVisitor(PhantomData))
        }
    }
    use std::error::Error;
    use std::fmt::Write as _;
    use std::time::{Duration, Instant};
    
    use legendary_octo_spork::{Money, process_csv};
    
    const CLIENT_COUNT: u32 = 1024;
    
    struct Workload {
        label: &'static str,
        input: String,
        output: Vec<u8>,
        rows: u64,
    }
    
    fn account_output(counts: &[u32], chargeback: bool) -> Vec<u8> {
        let mut output = String::from("client,available,held,total,locked\n");
        for (client, count) in counts.iter().enumerate() {
            if *count == 0 {
                continue;
            }
            let total = Money(i64::from(*count) * 10_001 - if chargeback { 20_001 } else { 0 });
            writeln!(output, "{client},{total},0.0000,{total},{chargeback}")
                .expect("failed to format benchmark output");
        }
        output.into_bytes()
    }
    
    fn deposits(rows: u32) -> Workload {
        let mut input = String::with_capacity(rows as usize * 32);
        input.push_str("type,client,txid,amount\n");
        let mut counts = vec![0; CLIENT_COUNT as usize];
        for id in 0..rows {
            let client = id % CLIENT_COUNT;
            writeln!(input, "deposit,{client},{id},1.0001").expect("failed to format benchmark input");
            counts[client as usize] += 1;
        }
        Workload {
            label: "deposits",
            input,
            output: account_output(&counts, false),
            rows: u64::from(rows),
        }
    }
    
    fn mixed(groups: u32) -> Workload {
        let mut input = String::with_capacity(groups as usize * 100);
        input.push_str("type,client,txid,amount\n");
        let mut counts = vec![0; CLIENT_COUNT as usize];
        let mut last_ids = vec![0; CLIENT_COUNT as usize];
        for group in 0..groups {
            let client = group % CLIENT_COUNT;
            let id = group * 2;
            writeln!(input, "deposit,{client},{id},2.0001").expect("failed to format benchmark input");
            writeln!(input, "withdrawal,{client},{},1.0000", id + 1)
                .expect("failed to format benchmark input");
            writeln!(input, "dispute,{client},{id},").expect("failed to format benchmark input");
            writeln!(input, "resolve,{client},{id},").expect("failed to format benchmark input");
            counts[client as usize] += 1;
            last_ids[client as usize] = id;
        }
        let mut rows = u64::from(groups) * 4;
        for (client, count) in counts.iter().enumerate() {
            if *count == 0 {
                continue;
            }
            let id = last_ids[client];
            writeln!(input, "dispute,{client},{id},").expect("failed to format benchmark input");
            writeln!(input, "chargeback,{client},{id},").expect("failed to format benchmark input");
            rows += 2;
        }
        Workload {
            label: "mixed",
            input,
            output: account_output(&counts, true),
            rows,
        }
    }
    
    fn execute(workload: &Workload) -> Duration {
        let mut output = Vec::new();
        let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
        let start = Instant::now();
        process_csv(workload.input.as_bytes(), &mut output, &mut diagnostics)
            .expect("failed to process benchmark workload");
        let duration = start.elapsed();
        assert_eq!(output, workload.output, "incorrect benchmark balances");
        assert!(diagnostics.is_empty(), "invalid benchmark transactions");
        duration
    }
    
    fn measure(workload: Workload, rounds: usize) {
        execute(&workload);
        let mut durations: Vec<_> = (0..rounds).map(|_| execute(&workload)).collect();
        durations.sort_unstable();
        let seconds = durations[durations.len() / 2].as_secs_f64();
        println!(
            "{}: rows={} median_seconds={seconds:.6} rows_per_second={:.0} mib_per_second={:.2}",
            workload.label,
            workload.rows,
            workload.rows as f64 / seconds,
            workload.input.len() as f64 / (1024.0 * 1024.0) / seconds
        );
    }
    
    fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> {
        let rows: u32 = std::env::var("TX_BENCH_ROWS")
            .ok()
            .map(|value| value.parse())
            .transpose()?
            .unwrap_or(1_000_000);
        let rounds: usize = std::env::var("TX_BENCH_ROUNDS")
            .ok()
            .map(|value| value.parse())
            .transpose()?
            .unwrap_or(5);
        if rows == 0 || rounds == 0 {
            return Err("benchmark rows and rounds must exceed zero".into());
        }
        measure(deposits(rows), rounds);
        measure(mixed((rows / 4).max(1)), rounds);
        Ok(())
    }

    pub enum MoneyError {
        Syntax,
        Precision,
        Overflow,
    }
    
    impl fmt::Display for MoneyError {
        fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
            formatter.write_str(match self {
                Self::Syntax => "amount must contain decimal digits with an optional minus sign",
                Self::Precision => "amount exceeds four decimal places",
                Self::Overflow => "amount exceeds the numeric range",
            })
        }
    }
    
    impl std::error::Error for MoneyError {}
    
    impl<Value: MoneyValue> FromStr for Money<Value> {
        type Err = MoneyError;
    
        fn from_str(text: &str) -> Result<Self, Self::Err> {
            let (negative, digits) = match text.strip_prefix('-') {
                Some(digits) => (true, digits),
                None => (false, text),
            };
            let (whole, fraction) = match digits.split_once('.') {
                Some((whole, fraction)) if !fraction.is_empty() => (whole, fraction),
                Some(_) => return Err(MoneyError::Syntax),
                None => (digits, ""),
            };
            if whole.is_empty() {
                return Err(MoneyError::Syntax);
            }
            if fraction.len() > MONEY_PRECISION as usize {
                return Err(MoneyError::Precision);
            }
            let mut minor_units = Value::ZERO;
            let ten = Value::from(10);
            for digit in whole.bytes().chain(fraction.bytes()) {
                if !digit.is_ascii_digit() {
                    return Err(MoneyError::Syntax);
                }
                let digit_value = Value::from(u16::from(digit - b'0'));
                minor_units = minor_units
                    .checked_mul(ten)
                    .and_then(|value| {
                        if negative {
                            value.checked_sub(digit_value)
                        } else {
                            value.checked_add(digit_value)
                        }
                    })
                    .ok_or(MoneyError::Overflow)?;
            }
            for _ in fraction.len()..MONEY_PRECISION as usize {
                minor_units = minor_units.checked_mul(ten).ok_or(MoneyError::Overflow)?;
            }
            Ok(Self(minor_units))
        }
    }
    
    impl<Value: MoneyValue> fmt::Display for Money<Value> {
        fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
            let scale = Value::from(MONEY_SCALE);
            let mut whole = self.0 / scale;
            let mut fraction = self.0 % scale;
            if self.0 < Value::ZERO {
                formatter.write_str("-")?;
                whole = Value::ZERO.checked_sub(whole).ok_or(fmt::Error)?;
                fraction = Value::ZERO.checked_sub(fraction).ok_or(fmt::Error)?;
            }
            write!(
                formatter,
                "{whole}.{fraction:0width$}",
                width = MONEY_PRECISION as usize
            )
        }
    }

        fn serialize<Output: Serializer>(

    }

        fn visit_str<Error: de::Error>(self, value: &str) -> Result<Self::Value, Error> {

        fn deserialize<Input: Deserializer<'input>>(deserializer: Input) -> Result<Self, Input::Error> {

    pub struct ClientInfo<Value> {
        id: ClientId,
        total: Money<Value>,
        on_hold: Money<Value>,
        lock: bool,

    impl<Value: MoneyValue> ClientInfo<Value> {
        fn new(id: ClientId) -> Self {
            Self {
                id,
                total: Money(Value::ZERO),
                on_hold: Money(Value::ZERO),
                lock: false,
            }
        }
    
        pub fn id(&self) -> ClientId {
            self.id
        }
    
        pub fn total(&self) -> Money<Value> {
            self.total
        }
    
        pub fn on_hold(&self) -> Money<Value> {
            self.on_hold
        }
    
        pub fn available(&self) -> Money<Value> {
            Money(
                self.total
                    .0
                    .checked_sub(self.on_hold.0)
                    .expect("account balance overflow"),
            )
        }
    
        pub fn lock(&self) -> bool {
            self.lock
        }
    
        fn update(&mut self, total: Value, on_hold: Value) -> Result<(), TransactionError> {
            total
                .checked_sub(on_hold)
                .ok_or(TransactionError::Overflow)?;
            self.total = Money(total);
            self.on_hold = Money(on_hold);
            Ok(())
        }
    }

                Self::DuplicateTransaction => "transaction ID already exists",
                Self::AccountLock => "account lock prevents transactions",
                Self::InsufficientFunds => "insufficient available funds",
                Self::UnknownTransaction => "transaction does not exist",
                Self::ClientMismatch => "transaction belongs to another client",
                Self::WithdrawalControl => {
                    "withdrawal does not support disputes, resolves, or chargebacks"
                }
                Self::DisputeConflict => "transaction has an active dispute or chargeback",

    #[derive(Debug)]
    pub struct Engine<Value = i64> {
        clients: HashMap<ClientId, ClientInfo<Value>>,
        transactions: HashMap<TxId, TxRecord<Value>>,
    }
    
    impl<Value> Default for Engine<Value> {
        fn default() -> Self {
            Self {
                clients: HashMap::new(),
                transactions: HashMap::new(),
            }
        }
    }
    
    impl<Value: MoneyValue> Engine<Value> {
        pub fn clients(&self) -> &HashMap<ClientId, ClientInfo<Value>> {
            &self.clients
        }
    
        pub fn into_clients(self) -> HashMap<ClientId, ClientInfo<Value>> {
            self.clients
        }
    
        pub fn apply(&mut self, transaction: Transaction<Value>) -> Result<(), TransactionError> {
            let (amount, deposit) = match transaction.ty {
                TxType::Deposit(amount) => (amount.0, true),
                TxType::Withdrawal(amount) => (amount.0, false),
                _ => return self.apply_control(transaction),
            };
            if amount < Value::ZERO {
                return Err(TransactionError::NegativeAmount);
            }
            let entry = match self.transactions.entry(transaction.id) {
                Entry::Vacant(entry) => entry,
                Entry::Occupied(_) => return Err(TransactionError::DuplicateTransaction),
            };
            let account = self
                .clients
                .entry(transaction.client_id)
                .or_insert_with(|| ClientInfo::new(transaction.client_id));
            if account.lock {
                return Err(TransactionError::AccountLock);
            }
            let (total, status) = if deposit {
                (
                    account
                        .total
                        .0
                        .checked_add(amount)
                        .ok_or(TransactionError::Overflow)?,
                    TxStatus::Deposit(Money(amount)),
                )
            } else {
                if account.available().0 < amount {
                    return Err(TransactionError::InsufficientFunds);
                }
                (
                    account
                        .total
                        .0
                        .checked_sub(amount)
                        .ok_or(TransactionError::Overflow)?,
                    TxStatus::Withdrawal,
                )
            };
            account.update(total, account.on_hold.0)?;
            entry.insert(TxRecord {
                client_id: transaction.client_id,
                status,
            });
            Ok(())
        }
    
        fn apply_control(&mut self, transaction: Transaction<Value>) -> Result<(), TransactionError> {
            let record = self
                .transactions
                .get_mut(&transaction.id)
                .ok_or(TransactionError::UnknownTransaction)?;
            if record.client_id != transaction.client_id {
                return Err(TransactionError::ClientMismatch);
            }
            let account = self
                .clients
                .get_mut(&transaction.client_id)
                .expect("transaction account missing");
            if account.lock {
                return Err(TransactionError::AccountLock);
            }
            let (total, on_hold, status, lock) = match (transaction.ty, record.status) {
                (TxType::Dispute, TxStatus::Deposit(amount)) => (
                    account.total.0,
                    account
                        .on_hold
                        .0
                        .checked_add(amount.0)
                        .ok_or(TransactionError::Overflow)?,
                    TxStatus::Dispute(amount),
                    false,
                ),
                (TxType::Resolve, TxStatus::Dispute(amount)) => (
                    account.total.0,
                    account
                        .on_hold
                        .0
                        .checked_sub(amount.0)
                        .ok_or(TransactionError::Overflow)?,
                    TxStatus::Deposit(amount),
                    false,
                ),
                (TxType::Chargeback, TxStatus::Dispute(amount)) => (
                    account
                        .total
                        .0
                        .checked_sub(amount.0)
                        .ok_or(TransactionError::Overflow)?,
                    account
                        .on_hold
                        .0
                        .checked_sub(amount.0)
                        .ok_or(TransactionError::Overflow)?,
                    TxStatus::Chargeback,
                    true,
                ),
                (_, TxStatus::Withdrawal) => return Err(TransactionError::WithdrawalControl),
                (TxType::Dispute, _) => return Err(TransactionError::DisputeConflict),
                _ => return Err(TransactionError::NoDispute),
            };
            account.update(total, on_hold)?;
            account.lock = lock;
            record.status = status;
            Ok(())
        }
    }

    pub enum ProcessError<InputError> {
        Input(InputError),

    }
    
    impl<InputError: fmt::Display> fmt::Display for ProcessError<InputError> {
        fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
            match self {
                Self::Input(error) => write!(formatter, "failed to read transaction: {error}"),
                Self::Diagnostics(error) => write!(formatter, "failed to write diagnostics: {error}"),
            }
        }
    }
    
    impl<InputError: std::error::Error + 'static> std::error::Error for ProcessError<InputError> {
        fn source(&self) -> Option<&(dyn std::error::Error + 'static)> {
            match self {

            }
        }
    }
    
    pub fn process_txs<Value, Input, InputError, Diagnostics>(
        transactions: Input,
        diagnostics: Diagnostics,
    ) -> Result<HashMap<ClientId, ClientInfo<Value>>, ProcessError<InputError>>
    where
        Value: MoneyValue,
        Input: IntoIterator<Item = Result<Transaction<Value>, InputError>>,
        Diagnostics: Write,
    {
        let mut engine = Engine::default();
        let mut diagnostics = BufWriter::with_capacity(IO_BUFFER_CAPACITY, diagnostics);
        for transaction in transactions {
            let transaction = match transaction {
                Ok(transaction) => transaction,
                Err(error) => {
                    diagnostics.flush().map_err(ProcessError::Diagnostics)?;
                    return Err(ProcessError::Input(error));
                }
            };
            if let Err(error) = engine.apply(transaction) {
                writeln!(
                    diagnostics,
                    "client {}, transaction {}: {error}",
                    *transaction.client_id, *transaction.id
                )
                .map_err(ProcessError::Diagnostics)?;
            }
        }
        diagnostics.flush().map_err(ProcessError::Diagnostics)?;
        Ok(engine.into_clients())
    }

            let mut reader = csv::ReaderBuilder::new()
                .trim(csv::Trim::All)
                .buffer_capacity(IO_BUFFER_CAPACITY)
                .from_reader(RetryReader(input));
            let headers = reader.byte_headers().map_err(InputError::Csv)?.clone();
            let columns: [&[u8]; 4] = [b"type", b"client", b"txid", b"amount"];
            if headers.len() != columns.len()
                || columns
                    .iter()
                    .any(|column| headers.iter().filter(|header| header == column).count() != 1)
            {
                return Err(InputError::Headers);
            }
            Ok(Self {
                reader,
                headers,
                record: csv::ByteRecord::with_capacity(128, 4),
                stop: false,
                value_type: PhantomData,
            })
        }
    
        fn read_transaction(&mut self) -> Result<Option<Transaction<Value>>, InputError> {
            if !self
                .reader
                .read_byte_record(&mut self.record)
                .map_err(InputError::Csv)?
            {
                return Ok(None);
            }
            let record: CsvTransaction<Value> = self
                .record
                .deserialize(Some(&self.headers))
                .map_err(InputError::Csv)?;
            let amount = || {
                record.amount.ok_or_else(|| InputError::MissingAmount {
                    line: self.record.position().map_or(0, csv::Position::line),
                })
            };
            let ty = match record.ty {
                CsvTxType::Deposit => TxType::Deposit(amount()?),
                CsvTxType::Withdrawal => TxType::Withdrawal(amount()?),
                CsvTxType::Dispute => TxType::Dispute,
                CsvTxType::Resolve => TxType::Resolve,
                CsvTxType::Chargeback => TxType::Chargeback,
            };
            Ok(Some(Transaction {
                ty,
                client_id: record.client,
                id: record.txid,
            }))
        }
    }
    
    impl<Input: Read, Value: MoneyValue> Iterator for CsvTransactions<Input, Value> {
        type Item = Result<Transaction<Value>, InputError>;
    
        fn next(&mut self) -> Option<Self::Item> {
            if self.stop {
                return None;
            }
            match self.read_transaction() {
                Ok(Some(transaction)) => Some(Ok(transaction)),
                Ok(None) => {
                    self.stop = true;
                    None
                }
                Err(error) => {
                    self.stop = true;
                    Some(Err(error))
                }
            }
        }
    }
    
    impl<Input: Read, Value: MoneyValue> FusedIterator for CsvTransactions<Input, Value> {}
    
    #[derive(Serialize)]
    #[serde(bound(serialize = "Value: MoneyValue"))]
    struct CsvClient<Value> {
        client: ClientId,
        available: Money<Value>,
        #[serde(rename = "held")]
        on_hold: Money<Value>,
        total: Money<Value>,
        #[serde(rename = "locked")]
        lock: bool,
    }
    
    pub fn write_clients<Value: MoneyValue, Output: Write>(
        clients: &HashMap<ClientId, ClientInfo<Value>>,
        output: Output,
    ) -> Result<(), CsvError> {
        let mut writer = csv::WriterBuilder::new()
            .has_headers(false)
            .buffer_capacity(IO_BUFFER_CAPACITY)
            .from_writer(output);
        writer
            .write_record(["client", "available", "held", "total", "locked"])
            .map_err(CsvError::Output)?;
        let mut clients: Vec<_> = clients.values().collect();
        clients.sort_unstable_by_key(|client| client.id());
        for client in clients {
            writer
                .serialize(CsvClient {
                    client: client.id(),
                    available: client.available(),
                    on_hold: client.on_hold(),
                    total: client.total(),
                    lock: client.lock(),
                })
                .map_err(CsvError::Output)?;
        }
        writer
            .flush()
            .map_err(|error| CsvError::Output(error.into()))
    }
    
    #[derive(Debug)]
    pub enum CsvError {
        Process(ProcessError<InputError>),
        Output(csv::Error),
    }
    
    impl fmt::Display for CsvError {
        fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
            match self {
                Self::Process(error) => error.fmt(formatter),
                Self::Output(error) => write!(formatter, "failed to write account CSV: {error}"),
            }
        }
    }
    
    impl std::error::Error for CsvError {
        fn source(&self) -> Option<&(dyn std::error::Error + 'static)> {
            match self {
                Self::Process(error) => Some(error),
                Self::Output(error) => Some(error),
            }
        }
    }
    
    pub fn process_csv<Input: Read, Output: Write, Diagnostics: Write>(
        input: Input,
        output: Output,
        diagnostics: Diagnostics,
    ) -> Result<(), CsvError> {
        let transactions = CsvTransactions::<_, i64>::new(input)
            .map_err(|error| CsvError::Process(ProcessError::Input(error)))?;
        let clients = process_txs(transactions, diagnostics).map_err(CsvError::Process)?;
        write_clients(&clients, output)
    }

    #[test]
    fn decimal_values_use_exact_minor_units() {
        for (text, minor_units, output) in [
            ("0", 0, "0.0000"),

    struct ShortStream<Stream> {
        inner: Stream,
        limit: usize,
    }
    
    impl<Stream: Read> Read for ShortStream<Stream> {
        fn read(&mut self, buffer: &mut [u8]) -> io::Result<usize> {
            let length = buffer.len().min(self.limit);
            self.inner.read(&mut buffer[..length])
        }
    }
    
    impl<Stream: Write> Write for ShortStream<Stream> {
        fn write(&mut self, buffer: &[u8]) -> io::Result<usize> {
            self.inner.write(&buffer[..buffer.len().min(self.limit)])
        }

## Assistant

`Money` now wraps `i64` directly. I removed the numeric type parameters, trait, macro, and `PhantomData`. The stream APIs still accept generic readers and writers.

All 36 remaining tests pass. I removed the two `i128`-only tests; the `i64` boundary and overflow checks remain. I’m reviewing the diff and running the release and lint checks.

     The peer must finish its input, for example with `shutdown(Shutdown::Write)`, before reading the account response. The integration suite checks this exchange over a real loopback TCP connection. For connections without an end of input, feed records to `Engine::apply` and use `write_clients` when the application requires a snapshot. These APIs use blocking I/O.
    
    -`Money<Value>` stores minor units, so `Money(12_345_i64)` represents `1.2345`. `MoneyValue` supplies checked integer operations. The library implements it for `i64` and `i128`; use `i128` for larger amounts while supporting negative balances. `CsvTransactions::<_, i128>`, `process_txs`, and `write_clients` support that type without changes to decimal parsing. `ClientId`, `TxId`, and `Money` implement `Deref`. Transaction variants require an amount for deposits and withdrawals, and account fields remain private so callers cannot bypass balance checks.
    +`Money(i64)` stores minor units, so `Money(12_345)` represents `1.2345`. Parsing and balance updates use checked `i64` arithmetic. `ClientId`, `TxId`, and `Money` implement `Deref`. Transaction variants require an amount for deposits and withdrawals, and account fields remain private so callers cannot bypass balance checks.
    
     The processor does not collect input records. It reuses CSV record storage and uses 64 KiB buffers for input, output, and diagnostics. The reader retries interrupted reads before CSV parsing. Processing takes expected linear time in the number of records, plus account sorting. Memory grows with client count, unique successful monetary transactions, and the largest CSV record. The engine retains transaction history for duplicate detection, later disputes, and withdrawal validation. Repeated dispute and resolve operations reuse an existing history entry.

    fn run() -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> {
        let mut arguments = std::env::args_os().skip(1);
        let path = arguments
            .next()
            .ok_or("usage: legendary-octo-spork <input.csv>")?;
        if arguments.next().is_some() {
            return Err("usage: legendary-octo-spork <input.csv>".into());
        }
        let input = File::open(&path).map_err(|error| {
            io::Error::new(
                error.kind(),
                format!("failed to open '{}': {error}", Path::new(&path).display()),
            )
        })?;
        process_csv(input, io::stdout().lock(), io::stderr().lock())?;
        Ok(())
    }
    
    fn main() -> ExitCode {
        match run() {
            Ok(()) => ExitCode::SUCCESS,
            Err(error) => {
                let _ = writeln!(io::stderr().lock(), "error: {error}");
                ExitCode::FAILURE
            }
        }
    }

            }
        }
    }

    struct RetryReader<Input>(Input);
    
    impl<Input: Read> Read for RetryReader<Input> {
        fn read(&mut self, buffer: &mut [u8]) -> io::Result<usize> {
            loop {
                match self.0.read(buffer) {
                    Err(error) if error.kind() == io::ErrorKind::Interrupted => continue,
                    result => return result,
                }
            }
        }
    }
    
    pub struct CsvTransactions<Input> {
        reader: csv::Reader<RetryReader<Input>>,
        headers: csv::ByteRecord,
        record: csv::ByteRecord,
        stop: bool,
    }
    
    impl<Input: Read> CsvTransactions<Input> {
        pub fn new(input: Input) -> Result<Self, InputError> {
            let mut reader = csv::ReaderBuilder::new()
                .trim(csv::Trim::All)
                .buffer_capacity(IO_BUFFER_CAPACITY)
                .from_reader(RetryReader(input));
            let headers = reader.byte_headers().map_err(InputError::Csv)?.clone();
            let columns: [&[u8]; 4] = [b"type", b"client", b"txid", b"amount"];
            if headers.len() != columns.len()
                || columns
                    .iter()
                    .any(|column| headers.iter().filter(|header| header == column).count() != 1)
            {
                return Err(InputError::Headers);
            }
            Ok(Self {
                reader,
                headers,
                record: csv::ByteRecord::with_capacity(128, 4),
                stop: false,
            })
        }
    
        fn read_transaction(&mut self) -> Result<Option<Transaction>, InputError> {
            if !self
                .reader
                .read_byte_record(&mut self.record)
                .map_err(InputError::Csv)?
            {
                return Ok(None);
            }
            let record: CsvTransaction = self
                .record
                .deserialize(Some(&self.headers))
                .map_err(InputError::Csv)?;
            let amount = || {
                record.amount.ok_or_else(|| InputError::MissingAmount {
                    line: self.record.position().map_or(0, csv::Position::line),
                })
            };
            let ty = match record.ty {
                CsvTxType::Deposit => TxType::Deposit(amount()?),
                CsvTxType::Withdrawal => TxType::Withdrawal(amount()?),
                CsvTxType::Dispute => TxType::Dispute,
                CsvTxType::Resolve => TxType::Resolve,
                CsvTxType::Chargeback => TxType::Chargeback,
            };
            Ok(Some(Transaction {
                ty,
                client_id: record.client,
                id: record.txid,
            }))
        }
    }
    
    impl<Input: Read> Iterator for CsvTransactions<Input> {
        type Item = Result<Transaction, InputError>;
    
        fn next(&mut self) -> Option<Self::Item> {
            if self.stop {
                return None;
            }
            match self.read_transaction() {
                Ok(Some(transaction)) => Some(Ok(transaction)),
                Ok(None) => {
                    self.stop = true;
                    None
                }
                Err(error) => {
                    self.stop = true;
                    Some(Err(error))
                }
            }
        }
    }
    
    impl<Input: Read> FusedIterator for CsvTransactions<Input> {}
    
    #[derive(Serialize)]
    struct CsvClient {
        client: ClientId,
        available: Money,
        #[serde(rename = "held")]
        on_hold: Money,
        total: Money,
        #[serde(rename = "locked")]
        lock: bool,
    }
    
    pub fn write_clients<Output: Write>(
        clients: &HashMap<ClientId, ClientInfo>,
        output: Output,
    ) -> Result<(), CsvError> {
        let mut writer = csv::WriterBuilder::new()
            .has_headers(false)
            .buffer_capacity(IO_BUFFER_CAPACITY)
            .from_writer(output);
        writer
            .write_record(["client", "available", "held", "total", "locked"])
            .map_err(CsvError::Output)?;
        let mut clients: Vec<_> = clients.values().collect();
        clients.sort_unstable_by_key(|client| client.id());
        for client in clients {
            writer
                .serialize(CsvClient {
                    client: client.id(),
                    available: client.available(),
                    on_hold: client.on_hold(),
                    total: client.total(),
                    lock: client.lock(),
                })
                .map_err(CsvError::Output)?;
        }
        writer
            .flush()
            .map_err(|error| CsvError::Output(error.into()))
    }
    
    #[derive(Debug)]
    pub enum CsvError {
        Process(ProcessError<InputError>),
        Output(csv::Error),
    }
    
    impl fmt::Display for CsvError {
        fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
            match self {
                Self::Process(error) => error.fmt(formatter),
                Self::Output(error) => write!(formatter, "failed to write account CSV: {error}"),
            }
        }
    }
    
    impl std::error::Error for CsvError {
        fn source(&self) -> Option<&(dyn std::error::Error + 'static)> {
            match self {
                Self::Process(error) => Some(error),
                Self::Output(error) => Some(error),
            }
        }
    }
    
    pub fn process_csv<Input: Read, Output: Write, Diagnostics: Write>(
        input: Input,
        output: Output,
        diagnostics: Diagnostics,
    ) -> Result<(), CsvError> {
        let transactions = CsvTransactions::new(input)
            .map_err(|error| CsvError::Process(ProcessError::Input(error)))?;
        let clients = process_txs(transactions, diagnostics).map_err(CsvError::Process)?;
        write_clients(&clients, output)
    }

    #[derive(Clone, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
    pub struct ClientInfo {
        id: ClientId,
        total: Money,
        on_hold: Money,
        lock: bool,
    }
    
    impl ClientInfo {
        fn new(id: ClientId) -> Self {
            Self {
                id,
                total: Money(0),
                on_hold: Money(0),
                lock: false,
            }
        }
    
        pub fn id(&self) -> ClientId {
            self.id
        }
    
        pub fn total(&self) -> Money {
            self.total
        }
    
        pub fn on_hold(&self) -> Money {
            self.on_hold
        }
    
        pub fn available(&self) -> Money {
            Money(
                self.total
                    .0
                    .checked_sub(self.on_hold.0)
                    .expect("account balance overflow"),
            )
        }
    
        pub fn lock(&self) -> bool {
            self.lock
        }
    
        fn update(&mut self, total: i64, on_hold: i64) -> Result<(), TransactionError> {
            total
                .checked_sub(on_hold)
                .ok_or(TransactionError::Overflow)?;
            self.total = Money(total);
            self.on_hold = Money(on_hold);
            Ok(())
        }
    }

    #[derive(Debug)]

    #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
    pub enum TransactionError {
        NegativeAmount,
        DuplicateTransaction,
        AccountLock,
        InsufficientFunds,
        UnknownTransaction,
        ClientMismatch,
        WithdrawalControl,
        DisputeConflict,
        NoDispute,
        Overflow,
    }
    
    impl fmt::Display for TransactionError {
        fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
            formatter.write_str(match self {
                Self::NegativeAmount => "amount must not be negative",
                Self::DuplicateTransaction => "transaction ID already exists",
                Self::AccountLock => "account lock prevents transactions",
                Self::InsufficientFunds => "insufficient available funds",
                Self::UnknownTransaction => "transaction does not exist",
                Self::ClientMismatch => "transaction belongs to another client",
                Self::WithdrawalControl => {
                    "withdrawal does not support disputes, resolves, or chargebacks"
                }
                Self::DisputeConflict => "transaction has an active dispute or chargeback",
                Self::NoDispute => "transaction requires an active dispute",
                Self::Overflow => "account balance exceeds the numeric range",
            })
        }
    }
    
    impl std::error::Error for TransactionError {}
    
    #[derive(Debug, Default)]
    pub struct Engine {
        clients: HashMap<ClientId, ClientInfo>,
        transactions: HashMap<TxId, TxRecord>,
    }
    
    impl Engine {
        pub fn clients(&self) -> &HashMap<ClientId, ClientInfo> {
            &self.clients
        }
    
        pub fn into_clients(self) -> HashMap<ClientId, ClientInfo> {
            self.clients
        }
    
        pub fn apply(&mut self, transaction: Transaction) -> Result<(), TransactionError> {
            let (amount, deposit) = match transaction.ty {
                TxType::Deposit(amount) => (amount.0, true),
                TxType::Withdrawal(amount) => (amount.0, false),
                _ => return self.apply_control(transaction),
            };
            if amount < 0 {
                return Err(TransactionError::NegativeAmount);
            }
            let entry = match self.transactions.entry(transaction.id) {
                Entry::Vacant(entry) => entry,
                Entry::Occupied(_) => return Err(TransactionError::DuplicateTransaction),
            };
            let account = self
                .clients
                .entry(transaction.client_id)
                .or_insert_with(|| ClientInfo::new(transaction.client_id));
            if account.lock {
                return Err(TransactionError::AccountLock);
            }
            let (total, status) = if deposit {
                (
                    account
                        .total
                        .0
                        .checked_add(amount)
                        .ok_or(TransactionError::Overflow)?,
                    TxStatus::Deposit(Money(amount)),
                )
            } else {
                if account.available().0 < amount {
                    return Err(TransactionError::InsufficientFunds);
                }
                (
                    account
                        .total
                        .0
                        .checked_sub(amount)
                        .ok_or(TransactionError::Overflow)?,
                    TxStatus::Withdrawal,
                )
            };
            account.update(total, account.on_hold.0)?;
            entry.insert(TxRecord {
                client_id: transaction.client_id,
                status,
            });
            Ok(())
        }
    
        fn apply_control(&mut self, transaction: Transaction) -> Result<(), TransactionError> {
            let record = self
                .transactions
                .get_mut(&transaction.id)
                .ok_or(TransactionError::UnknownTransaction)?;
            if record.client_id != transaction.client_id {
                return Err(TransactionError::ClientMismatch);
            }
            let account = self
                .clients
                .get_mut(&transaction.client_id)
                .expect("transaction account missing");
            if account.lock {
                return Err(TransactionError::AccountLock);
            }
            let (total, on_hold, status, lock) = match (transaction.ty, record.status) {
                (TxType::Dispute, TxStatus::Deposit(amount)) => (
                    account.total.0,
                    account
                        .on_hold
                        .0
                        .checked_add(amount.0)
                        .ok_or(TransactionError::Overflow)?,
                    TxStatus::Dispute(amount),
                    false,
                ),
                (TxType::Resolve, TxStatus::Dispute(amount)) => (
                    account.total.0,
                    account
                        .on_hold
                        .0
                        .checked_sub(amount.0)
                        .ok_or(TransactionError::Overflow)?,
                    TxStatus::Deposit(amount),
                    false,
                ),
                (TxType::Chargeback, TxStatus::Dispute(amount)) => (
                    account
                        .total
                        .0
                        .checked_sub(amount.0)
                        .ok_or(TransactionError::Overflow)?,
                    account
                        .on_hold
                        .0
                        .checked_sub(amount.0)
                        .ok_or(TransactionError::Overflow)?,
                    TxStatus::Chargeback,
                    true,
                ),
                (_, TxStatus::Withdrawal) => return Err(TransactionError::WithdrawalControl),
                (TxType::Dispute, _) => return Err(TransactionError::DisputeConflict),
                _ => return Err(TransactionError::NoDispute),
            };
            account.update(total, on_hold)?;
            account.lock = lock;
            record.status = status;
            Ok(())
        }
    }
    
    #[derive(Debug)]
    pub enum ProcessError<InputError> {
        Input(InputError),
        Diagnostics(io::Error),
    }
    
    impl<InputError: fmt::Display> fmt::Display for ProcessError<InputError> {
        fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
            match self {
                Self::Input(error) => write!(formatter, "failed to read transaction: {error}"),
                Self::Diagnostics(error) => write!(formatter, "failed to write diagnostics: {error}"),
            }
        }
    }
    
    impl<InputError: std::error::Error + 'static> std::error::Error for ProcessError<InputError> {
        fn source(&self) -> Option<&(dyn std::error::Error + 'static)> {
            match self {
                Self::Input(error) => Some(error),
                Self::Diagnostics(error) => Some(error),
            }
        }
    }
    
    pub fn process_txs<Input, InputError, Diagnostics>(
        transactions: Input,
        diagnostics: Diagnostics,
    ) -> Result<HashMap<ClientId, ClientInfo>, ProcessError<InputError>>
    where
        Input: IntoIterator<Item = Result<Transaction, InputError>>,
        Diagnostics: Write,
    {
        let mut engine = Engine::default();
        let mut diagnostics = BufWriter::with_capacity(IO_BUFFER_CAPACITY, diagnostics);
        for transaction in transactions {
            let transaction = match transaction {
                Ok(transaction) => transaction,
                Err(error) => {
                    diagnostics.flush().map_err(ProcessError::Diagnostics)?;
                    return Err(ProcessError::Input(error));
                }
            };
            if let Err(error) = engine.apply(transaction) {
                writeln!(
                    diagnostics,
                    "client {}, transaction {}: {error}",
                    *transaction.client_id, *transaction.id
                )
                .map_err(ProcessError::Diagnostics)?;
            }
        }
        diagnostics.flush().map_err(ProcessError::Diagnostics)?;
        Ok(engine.into_clients())
    }

    Status: simplify pipeline error handling.

    Known facts: the current pipeline uses three wrapper enums with custom Display and Error implementations. Existing tests cover CSV failures, source failures, output and diagnostic write and flush failures, and empty account output after input failure.
    
    Decision: use anyhow Result and Context. Boxed errors need manual context wrappers to preserve the same operation and source information. Keep typed domain errors and the generic transaction iterator.
    
    Plan:
    1. Strengthen existing error checks for operation context and source preservation.
    2. Replace wrapper enums with anyhow, simplify the CLI, and update documentation.
    3. Review line reduction, run tests, formatting, and Clippy, update notes, and commit.

    mod ext {

        pub trait StdError {
            fn ext_context<C>(self, context: C) -> Error
            where
                C: Display + Send + Sync + 'static;
        }
    
        #[cfg(any(feature = "std", not(anyhow_no_core_error)))]
        impl<E> StdError for E
        where
            E: crate::StdError + Send + Sync + 'static,
        {
            fn ext_context<C>(self, context: C) -> Error
            where
                C: Display + Send + Sync + 'static,
            {
                let backtrace = backtrace_if_absent!(&self);
                Error::construct_from_context(context, self, backtrace)
            }
        }
    
        impl StdError for Error {
            fn ext_context<C>(self, context: C) -> Error
            where
                C: Display + Send + Sync + 'static,
            {
                self.context(context)
            }
        }
    }
    
    impl<T, E> Context<T, E> for Result<T, E>
    where
        E: ext::StdError + Send + Sync + 'static,
    {
        fn context<C>(self, context: C) -> Result<T, Error>
        where
            C: Display + Send + Sync + 'static,
        {
            // Not using map_err to save 2 useless frames off the captured backtrace
            // in ext_context.
            match self {
                Ok(ok) => Ok(ok),
                Err(error) => Err(error.ext_context(context)),
            }
        }
    
        fn with_context<C, F>(self, context: F) -> Result<T, Error>
        where
            C: Display + Send + Sync + 'static,
            F: FnOnce() -> C,
        {
            match self {
                Ok(ok) => Ok(ok),
                Err(error) => Err(error.ext_context(context())),
            }
        }
    }

    use std::fs::File;
    use std::io;
    use std::path::Path;
    
    use anyhow::{Context, Result, bail};
    use legendary_octo_spork::process_csv;
    
    fn main() -> Result<()> {
        let mut arguments = std::env::args_os().skip(1);
        let path = arguments
            .next()
            .context("usage: legendary-octo-spork <input.csv>")?;
        if arguments.next().is_some() {
            bail!("usage: legendary-octo-spork <input.csv>");
        }
        let input = File::open(&path)
            .with_context(|| format!("failed to open '{}'", Path::new(&path).display()))?;
        process_csv(input, io::stdout().lock(), io::stderr().lock())
    }

    use std::collections::HashMap;
    use std::io::{self, Read, Write};
    use std::iter::FusedIterator;
    
    use anyhow::{Context, Result, bail};
    use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
    
    use crate::{
        ClientId, ClientInfo, IO_BUFFER_CAPACITY, Money, Transaction, TxId, TxType, process_txs,
    };
    
    #[derive(Deserialize)]
    #[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
    enum CsvTxType {
        Deposit,
        Withdrawal,
        Dispute,
        Resolve,
        Chargeback,
    }
    
    #[derive(Deserialize)]
    struct CsvTransaction {
        #[serde(rename = "type")]
        ty: CsvTxType,
        client: ClientId,
        txid: TxId,
        amount: Option<Money>,
    }
    
    struct RetryReader<Input>(Input);
    
    impl<Input: Read> Read for RetryReader<Input> {
        fn read(&mut self, buffer: &mut [u8]) -> io::Result<usize> {
            loop {
                match self.0.read(buffer) {
                    Err(error) if error.kind() == io::ErrorKind::Interrupted => continue,
                    result => return result,
                }
            }
        }
    }
    
    pub struct CsvTransactions<Input> {
        reader: csv::Reader<RetryReader<Input>>,
        headers: csv::ByteRecord,
        record: csv::ByteRecord,
        stop: bool,
    }
    
    impl<Input: Read> CsvTransactions<Input> {
        pub fn new(input: Input) -> Result<Self> {
            let mut reader = csv::ReaderBuilder::new()
                .trim(csv::Trim::All)
                .buffer_capacity(IO_BUFFER_CAPACITY)
                .from_reader(RetryReader(input));
            let headers = reader.byte_headers().context("failed to read CSV")?.clone();
            let columns: [&[u8]; 4] = [b"type", b"client", b"txid", b"amount"];
            if headers.len() != columns.len()
                || columns
                    .iter()
                    .any(|column| headers.iter().filter(|header| header == column).count() != 1)
            {
                bail!("invalid CSV header: require type,client,txid,amount exactly once in any order");
            }
            Ok(Self {
                reader,
                headers,
                record: csv::ByteRecord::with_capacity(128, 4),
                stop: false,
            })
        }
    
        fn read_transaction(&mut self) -> Result<Option<Transaction>> {
            if !self.reader.read_byte_record(&mut self.record)? {
                return Ok(None);
            }
            let record: CsvTransaction = self.record.deserialize(Some(&self.headers))?;
            let amount = || {
                record.amount.with_context(|| {
                    format!(
                        "missing amount at CSV line {}: deposits and withdrawals require an amount",
                        self.record.position().map_or(0, csv::Position::line)
                    )
                })
            };
            let ty = match record.ty {
                CsvTxType::Deposit => TxType::Deposit(amount()?),
                CsvTxType::Withdrawal => TxType::Withdrawal(amount()?),
                CsvTxType::Dispute => TxType::Dispute,
                CsvTxType::Resolve => TxType::Resolve,
                CsvTxType::Chargeback => TxType::Chargeback,
            };
            Ok(Some(Transaction {
                ty,
                client_id: record.client,
                id: record.txid,
            }))
        }
    }
    
    impl<Input: Read> Iterator for CsvTransactions<Input> {
        type Item = Result<Transaction>;
    
        fn next(&mut self) -> Option<Self::Item> {
            if self.stop {
                return None;
            }
            match self.read_transaction().context("failed to read CSV") {
                Ok(Some(transaction)) => Some(Ok(transaction)),
                Ok(None) => {
                    self.stop = true;
                    None
                }
                Err(error) => {
                    self.stop = true;
                    Some(Err(error))
                }
            }
        }
    }
    
    impl<Input: Read> FusedIterator for CsvTransactions<Input> {}
    
    #[derive(Serialize)]
    struct CsvClient {
        client: ClientId,
        available: Money,
        #[serde(rename = "held")]
        on_hold: Money,
        total: Money,
        #[serde(rename = "locked")]
        lock: bool,
    }
    
    pub fn write_clients<Output: Write>(
        clients: &HashMap<ClientId, ClientInfo>,
        output: Output,
    ) -> Result<()> {
        let mut writer = csv::WriterBuilder::new()
            .has_headers(false)
            .buffer_capacity(IO_BUFFER_CAPACITY)
            .from_writer(output);
        writer
            .write_record(["client", "available", "held", "total", "locked"])
            .context("failed to write account CSV")?;
        let mut clients: Vec<_> = clients.values().collect();
        clients.sort_unstable_by_key(|client| client.id());
        for client in clients {
            writer
                .serialize(CsvClient {
                    client: client.id(),
                    available: client.available(),
                    on_hold: client.on_hold(),
                    total: client.total(),
                    lock: client.lock(),
                })
                .context("failed to write account CSV")?;
        }
        writer.flush().context("failed to write account CSV")
    }
    
    pub fn process_csv<Input: Read, Output: Write, Diagnostics: Write>(
        input: Input,
        output: Output,
        diagnostics: Diagnostics,
    ) -> Result<()> {
        let transactions = CsvTransactions::new(input)?;
        let clients = process_txs(transactions, diagnostics)?;
        write_clients(&clients, output)
    }
    [package]
    name = "legendary-octo-spork"
    version = "0.1.0"
    edition = "2024"
    
    [dependencies]
    anyhow = "1.0.104"
    csv = "1.4.0"
    serde = { version = "1.0.229", features = ["derive"] }

    name = "throughput"
    harness = false

## User

A couple more fixes: 1) If the first transaction on an account is withdrawal, an empty account is created and the error is returned by the engine. I think we shouldn't create the account in this case. 2) I don't think we need to store withdrawal transactions in memory. The only sense for that is duplicate ID detection, which was not a requirement; 3) Dispute transactions do not have the amount: they have the same id as the original deposit transaction, and the dispute is always for the full amount. Fix parser and simplify logic accordingly.

    struct ShortStream<Stream> {
        inner: Stream,
        limit: usize,
    }
    
    impl<Stream: Read> Read for ShortStream<Stream> {
        fn read(&mut self, buffer: &mut [u8]) -> io::Result<usize> {
            let length = buffer.len().min(self.limit);
            self.inner.read(&mut buffer[..length])
        }
    }
    
    impl<Stream: Write> Write for ShortStream<Stream> {
        fn write(&mut self, buffer: &[u8]) -> io::Result<usize> {
            self.inner.write(&buffer[..buffer.len().min(self.limit)])
        }
    
        fn flush(&mut self) -> io::Result<()> {
            self.inner.flush()
        }
    }
    
    #[test]
    fn partial_reads_and_writes_preserve_record_boundaries() {
        let input = ShortStream {

            limit: 1,
        };
        let mut output = Vec::new();
        let writer = ShortStream {
            inner: &mut output,
            limit: 2,
        };
        process_csv(input, writer, io::sink()).expect("failed to process partial stream operations");
        assert_eq!(
            output,
            b"client,available,held,total,locked\n1,1.0001,0.0000,1.0001,false\n"
        );
    }
    
    struct InterruptReader<Input> {
        input: Input,
        interrupt: bool,
    }
    
    impl<Input: Read> Read for InterruptReader<Input> {
        fn read(&mut self, buffer: &mut [u8]) -> io::Result<usize> {
            if self.interrupt {
                self.interrupt = false;
                return Err(io::ErrorKind::Interrupted.into());
            }
            self.interrupt = true;
            self.input.read(buffer)
        }
    }

    struct FaultWriter {
        flush_only: bool,
    }
    
    impl Write for FaultWriter {
        fn write(&mut self, buffer: &[u8]) -> io::Result<usize> {
            if self.flush_only {
                Ok(buffer.len())
            } else {
                Err(io::Error::other("write failure"))
            }
        }
    
        fn flush(&mut self) -> io::Result<()> {
            Err(io::Error::other("flush failure"))
        }
    }
