    use std::error::Error;
    use std::fmt::Write as _;
    use std::time::{Duration, Instant};
    
    use legendary_octo_spork::{Money, process_csv};
    
    const CLIENT_COUNT: u32 = 1024;
    
    struct Workload {
        label: &'static str,
        input: String,
        output: Vec<u8>,
        rows: u64,
    }
    
    fn account_output(counts: &[u32], chargeback: bool) -> Vec<u8> {
        let mut output = String::from("client,available,held,total,locked\n");
        for (client, count) in counts.iter().enumerate() {
            if *count == 0 {
                continue;
            }
            let total = Money(i64::from(*count) * 10_001 - if chargeback { 20_001 } else { 0 });
            writeln!(output, "{client},{total},0.0000,{total},{chargeback}")
                .expect("failed to format benchmark output");
        }
        output.into_bytes()
    }
    
    fn deposits(rows: u32) -> Workload {
        let mut input = String::with_capacity(rows as usize * 32);
        input.push_str("type,client,tx,amount\n");
        let mut counts = vec![0; CLIENT_COUNT as usize];
        for id in 0..rows {
            let client = id % CLIENT_COUNT;
            writeln!(input, "deposit,{client},{id},1.0001").expect("failed to format benchmark input");
            counts[client as usize] += 1;
        }
        Workload {
            label: "deposits",
            input,
            output: account_output(&counts, false),
            rows: u64::from(rows),
        }
    }
    
    fn mixed(groups: u32) -> Workload {
        let mut input = String::with_capacity(groups as usize * 100);
        input.push_str("type,client,tx,amount\n");
        let mut counts = vec![0; CLIENT_COUNT as usize];
        let mut last_ids = vec![0; CLIENT_COUNT as usize];
        for group in 0..groups {
            let client = group % CLIENT_COUNT;
            let id = group * 2;
            writeln!(input, "deposit,{client},{id},2.0001").expect("failed to format benchmark input");
            writeln!(input, "withdrawal,{client},{},1.0000", id + 1)
                .expect("failed to format benchmark input");
            writeln!(input, "dispute,{client},{id},").expect("failed to format benchmark input");
            writeln!(input, "resolve,{client},{id},").expect("failed to format benchmark input");
            counts[client as usize] += 1;
            last_ids[client as usize] = id;
        }
        let mut rows = u64::from(groups) * 4;
        for (client, count) in counts.iter().enumerate() {
            if *count == 0 {
                continue;
            }
            let id = last_ids[client];
            writeln!(input, "dispute,{client},{id},").expect("failed to format benchmark input");
            writeln!(input, "chargeback,{client},{id},").expect("failed to format benchmark input");
            rows += 2;
        }
        Workload {
            label: "mixed",
            input,
            output: account_output(&counts, true),
            rows,
        }
    }
    
    fn execute(workload: &Workload) -> Duration {
        let mut output = Vec::new();
        let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
        let start = Instant::now();
        process_csv(workload.input.as_bytes(), &mut output, &mut diagnostics)
            .expect("failed to process benchmark workload");
        let duration = start.elapsed();
        assert_eq!(output, workload.output, "incorrect benchmark balances");
        assert!(diagnostics.is_empty(), "invalid benchmark transactions");
        duration
    }
    
    fn measure(workload: Workload, rounds: usize) {
        execute(&workload);
        let mut durations: Vec<_> = (0..rounds).map(|_| execute(&workload)).collect();
        durations.sort_unstable();
        let seconds = durations[durations.len() / 2].as_secs_f64();
        println!(
            "{}: rows={} median_seconds={seconds:.6} rows_per_second={:.0} mib_per_second={:.2}",
            workload.label,
            workload.rows,
            workload.rows as f64 / seconds,
            workload.input.len() as f64 / (1024.0 * 1024.0) / seconds
        );
    }
    
    fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> {
        let rows: u32 = std::env::var("TX_BENCH_ROWS")
            .ok()
            .map(|value| value.parse())
            .transpose()?
            .unwrap_or(1_000_000);
        let rounds: usize = std::env::var("TX_BENCH_ROUNDS")
            .ok()
            .map(|value| value.parse())
            .transpose()?
            .unwrap_or(5);
        if rows == 0 || rounds == 0 {
            return Err("benchmark rows and rounds must exceed zero".into());
        }
        measure(deposits(rows), rounds);
        measure(mixed((rows / 4).max(1)), rounds);
        Ok(())
    }
    import argparse
    import json
    import os
    from pathlib import Path
    import statistics
    import subprocess
    import time
    
    
    def decimal(minor_units):
        magnitude = abs(minor_units)
        sign = "-" if minor_units < 0 else ""
        return f"{sign}{magnitude // 10_000}.{magnitude % 10_000:04}"
    
    
    def create_input(directory, workload, rows):
        path = directory / f"{workload}-{rows}.csv"
        with path.open("w", buffering=1024 * 1024) as stream:
            stream.write("type,client,tx,amount\n")
            if workload == "deposits":
                stream.writelines(f"deposit,{index % 1024},{index},1.0001\n" for index in range(rows))
            else:
                stream.write("deposit,1,1,1\n")
                stream.writelines(
                    f"{'dispute' if index % 2 == 0 else 'resolve'},1,1,\n"
                    for index in range(rows - 1)
                )
        output = "client,available,held,total,locked\n"
        if workload == "deposits":
            for client in range(min(rows, 1024)):
                count = (rows - 1 - client) // 1024 + 1
                total = decimal(count * 10_001)
                output += f"{client},{total},0.0000,{total},false\n"
        else:
            on_hold = rows % 2 == 0
            output += f"1,{'0.0000,1.0000' if on_hold else '1.0000,0.0000'},1.0000,false\n"
        return path, output.encode()
    
    
    def measure(binary, path, output, rounds):
        output_path = path.with_suffix(".output")
        diagnostic_path = path.with_suffix(".stderr")
        samples = []
        for _ in range(rounds):
            with output_path.open("wb") as stream, diagnostic_path.open("wb") as diagnostics:
                start = time.perf_counter()
                process = subprocess.Popen([str(binary), str(path)], stdout=stream, stderr=diagnostics)
                peak_rss_kib = 0
                status_path = Path(f"/proc/{process.pid}/status")
                while True:
                    child_pid, status, usage = os.wait4(process.pid, os.WNOHANG)
                    if child_pid != 0:
                        break
                    try:
                        for line in status_path.read_text().splitlines():
                            if line.startswith("VmHWM:"):
                                peak_rss_kib = max(peak_rss_kib, int(line.split()[1]))
                    except FileNotFoundError:
                        pass
                    time.sleep(0.001)
                seconds = time.perf_counter() - start
                process.returncode = os.waitstatus_to_exitcode(status)
            if process.returncode != 0:
                raise RuntimeError(diagnostic_path.read_text())
            if diagnostic_path.stat().st_size != 0 or output_path.read_bytes() != output:
                raise RuntimeError("incorrect benchmark output")
            samples.append({
                "seconds": seconds,
                "peak_rss_kib": peak_rss_kib,
                "resource_peak_rss_kib": usage.ru_maxrss,
            })
        return samples
    
    
    def main():
        parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
        parser.add_argument("--rows", nargs="+", type=int, default=[1_000_000, 4_000_000])
        parser.add_argument("--rounds", type=int, default=3)
        arguments = parser.parse_args()
        root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
        directory = root / "target/throughput-inputs"
        directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        binary = root / "target/release/legendary-octo-spork"
        results = []
        for workload in ["deposits", "disputes"]:
            for rows in arguments.rows:
                path, output = create_input(directory, workload, rows)
                samples = measure(binary, path, output, arguments.rounds)
                seconds = statistics.median(sample["seconds"] for sample in samples)
                result = {
                    "workload": workload,
                    "rows": rows,
                    "input_bytes": path.stat().st_size,
                    "median_seconds": seconds,
                    "rows_per_second": rows / seconds,
                    "peak_rss_kib": max(sample["peak_rss_kib"] for sample in samples),
                    "samples": samples,
                }
                results.append(result)
                print(json.dumps(result), flush=True)
        report = {
            "rustc": subprocess.check_output(["rustc", "--version"], text=True).strip(),
            "results": results,
        }
        (root / ".agent/worklog/throughput.json").write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2) + "\n")
    
    
    if __name__ == "__main__":
        main()
    ## Context management
    When the conversation grows long, the harness summarizes some or all of the current context and provides the summary plus any remaining unsummarized context in the next context window. Work continues from there. Do not wrap up early or hand off mid-task because of context length.
    Do not stop because the context or session is long.
    
    When you have enough information to act, act. Do not re-derive facts already established in the conversation. Do not reopen decisions the user already made. Do not describe options you will not pursue.
    If you must choose between options, give one recommendation. Do not list every option.
    
    ## Delivering work
    Do the work as requested. Act on the actual request. Do not act on guesses about the user's underlying motive. Deliver the requested scope. Do not narrow, widen, or change it without telling the user.
    When the request is ambiguous, make routine judgment calls yourself. Ask the user only when different interpretations would produce materially different work.
    If you find a real problem with the task as specified, state the concern in one or two sentences, then continue. Deliver the complete work under explicitly stated assumptions and list the important factors for the user.
    Finish the whole task, including the hard parts. Report completion only when the task is fully done. If part of the scope is blocked or problematic, finish every other part in full and state explicitly what you left out and why. Only the user may reduce the scope.
    Do not perform actions or changes that are clearly beyond the request.
    
    If you find an open question mid-task, first do all work that does not depend on the answer. For work that depends on the answer, either state your assumption or ask the user.
    A blocking question stops all work until the user answers. Ask a blocking question only when proceeding under any assumption would be unsafe, or when a wrong assumption would make the work useless.
    
    If you raise a concern and the user repeats or confirms the request, treat that as the user's decision, say so, and do the full request.
    Be fair and factual when resolving disagreements about the premises, scope, or approach of the work.
    
    Before ending your turn, check your last paragraph. If it is a plan, an analysis, a question, a list of next steps, or a promise about work you have not done ("I'll…", "let me know when…"), do that work now with tool calls.
    That includes retrying after errors and gathering missing information yourself.
    
    Before running a command that changes system state (such as restarts, deletes, or config edits), check that the evidence supports that specific action.
    A symptom that looks like a known failure may have a different cause.
    
    ## Define an explicit goal and work until you achieve it
    State the "Definition of Done" for the task explicitly and ask the user to approve it.
    You may stop working only when:
      a) the task is done and you have *explicitly* verified that, or
      b) you encounter an issue that *requires* user intervention.
    
    ## Plan before you act; never guess
    Analyze the task before you act. State assumptions explicitly and verify them. List what you know and what you do not know.
    Write a detailed step-by-step plan and present a summary to the user. If uncertain, *always* ask or investigate. Never guess.
    
    ## Don't be afraid to pivot when stuck
    When stuck, change the approach. Your plan may change midway as long as the result still achieves the goal.
    
    ## Verify that instructions make sense
    You may object to any instruction (including a *direct* one) *once* if you think it is a bad idea or you can suggest a better approach.
    Never agree to an instruction without evaluating it. Execute only when the instruction makes sense; otherwise ask for confirmation.
    
    ## IMPORTANT: Minimize AI slop; use plain, simple language
    Do not use invented shorthands or heavy jargon. Say what something actually is.
    Never use metaphors or rhetorical flourishes. Never anthropomorphize.
    For example, a file does not "sit" in a directory; it "exists" there ("sit" implies it could also "stand"). A problem does not "bite"; it "occurs" (a problem has no mouth).
    No proverb symmetry ("teams change, topics stay"). No balanced contrast ("is a copy, not a rewrite"). No novelist's diction ("enters", "the latter case"). No wordplay.
    Be concrete. Do not use vague imperatives like "name them", "belongs elsewhere" or "that's all it takes".
    Never use fancy vocabulary. Use dry, technical, non-literary words. For example:
      - do not say "carry"; say "continue"
      - do not say "load-bearing"; say "critical"
      - do not say "survives"; say "remains"
      - do not say "asked"; say "requested"
      - do not say "refuses"; say "rejects"
      - do not say "holds"; say "contains"
    Use direct, dry, technical language. Avoid phrases and names that read as sentences or narrate. For example:
      - do not say "asked to think"; say "thinking enabled"
      - do not say "what was checked, not assumed"; say "what I checked"
      - do not say "room to answer"; say "remaining capacity"
      - do not say "where it stopped"; say "stopping point"
      - do not say "for a reason worth writing down"; say "for an important reason"
      - do not say "was never written down"; say "was never documented"
    Write like a software engineer with no literary skill.
    Never use abstract, soft phrasing that does not say what something is, or that only passively refers to something.
    Never use passive voice. Use active voice. For example, do not say "the last message wasn't written down"; say "the last message doesn't exist".
    Cut filler. Never editorialize. Use simple structure and simple vocabulary.
    This applies to everything you output: messages to the user, strings in code, method names, variable names, commit messages, and your own notes and status files.
    Do not match existing style when it disagrees with these guidelines.
    
    ## IMPORTANT: Do not write code comments
    Never write code comments. Code must be understandable without them.
    
    ## Write readable code
    Write clean, readable code that a senior engineer can understand without comments.
    Do not use single-character variable names. Do not code golf.
    
    ## IMPORTANT: Use dry, simple, concrete, technical language in code
    When writing code all of the "minimize AI slop" rules apply.
    Name things in the simplest, purely technical language.
    The following words are FORBIDDEN and should NEVER be used in code nor in any message in code: `ran`, `landed`, `land`, `given`, `give`, `settled`, `settle`, `held`, `holds`, `holding`, `says`, `names`, `named`, `reach`, `reaches`, `keep`, `keeps`, etc.
    Never use past participle in code.
    Always name things in *concrete* terms, for example:
      - do not write "written_at"; write "write_timestamp"
      - do not name a field "was" or "original"; write what it actually was, for example, "previous_name"
    
    ## Prefer integration tests over unit tests
    When possible write tests which test the high level behavior.
    Do not write tests which just naively weld the implementation in-place.
    A good test checks the end result without enforcing the exact algorithm, and doesn't fail when the algorithm changes.
    A bad test fails when the algorithm changes, even though the end result is the same.
    
    ## Practice test-driven development
    When possible, write a failing test first, then implement the fix.
    
    ## Tests must make sense and be thorough
    A test must document *why* the behavior matters. Documenting only *what* should happen is not enough.
    When you read an existing test, determine *why* it checks what it checks, and account for that when you change it.
    A test must fail when the business logic changes.
    Not everything must be tested. Irrelevant details do not need tests.
    
    ## IMPORTANT: Fix the root cause, not the symptom
    When fixing a bug, figure out what is its root cause, not just what directly caused it.
    Is the issue you're fixing a consequence of a particular architectural decision?
    Is there a more *fundamental* fix you could apply which not only fixes this issue, but also either fixes similar issues, or prevents the issue from reappearing in the future?
    Figure out *if* there is a fundamental root cause to what you're fixing, and what that root cause is.
    NEVER patch the symptoms when a root cause exists.
    When in doubt, ask the user to decide.
    
    ## Review and simplify your code
    After you write code, review it and simplify it. The less lines of code the better.
    Review the changes for AI slop, and deslop it before committing.
    
    ## Review subagents' work
    Always review and deslop subagent's work.
    
    ## Make small commits
    Make small, self-contained commits.
    Never `git push`; I review and rebase the full history and push myself.
    Commit messages exist so that I can review your work. Keep them *short* and single-line.
    
    ## Language-specific guidelines: Rust
    When writing Rust:
      - treat the `expect` message as an assertion failure message; do *not* state what was expected; for example, instead of `expect("JSON is valid")` write `expect("invalid JSON")`
      - chained error messages should always start with a lowercase letter; for example, instead of `.map_err(|error| format!("Failed to open '{path}': {path}"))` write `.map_err(|error| format!("failed to open '{path}': {path}"))`

      - use newtypes when appropriate
      - IMPORTANT: make illegal states unrepresentable
    
    ## Maintain an `.agent` directory
    Create and maintain an `.agent` directory for your exclusive use. Everything outside `.agent` is for humans.
    
    `.agent` must contain at least the following. You may add more as needed.
      - `.agent/worklog/` -- status, handoff, and worklog documents.

      - `.agent/MEMORY.md` -- a short index of `.agent/memory/` so that the next agent can find what it needs.

    #[derive(Clone, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
    pub struct ClientInfo {
        id: ClientId,
        total: Money,
        on_hold: Money,
        lock: bool,
    }
    
    impl ClientInfo {
        fn new(id: ClientId) -> Self {
            Self {
                id,
                total: Money(0),
                on_hold: Money(0),
                lock: false,
            }
        }
    
        pub fn id(&self) -> ClientId {
            self.id
        }
    
        pub fn total(&self) -> Money {
            self.total
        }
    
        pub fn on_hold(&self) -> Money {
            self.on_hold
        }
    
        pub fn available(&self) -> Money {
            Money(
                self.total
                    .0
                    .checked_sub(self.on_hold.0)
                    .expect("account balance overflow"),
            )
        }
    
        pub fn lock(&self) -> bool {
            self.lock
        }
    
        fn update(&mut self, total: i64, on_hold: i64) -> Result<(), TransactionError> {
            total
                .checked_sub(on_hold)
                .ok_or(TransactionError::Overflow)?;
            self.total = Money(total);
            self.on_hold = Money(on_hold);
            Ok(())
        }
    }
    
    #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
    enum TxStatus {
        Deposit(Money),
        Dispute(Money),
        Withdrawal,
        Chargeback,
    }
    
    #[derive(Debug)]
    struct TxRecord {
        client_id: ClientId,
        status: TxStatus,
    }
    
    #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
    pub enum TransactionError {
        NegativeAmount,
        DuplicateTransaction,
        AccountLock,
        InsufficientFunds,
        UnknownTransaction,
        ClientMismatch,
        WithdrawalControl,
        DisputeConflict,
        NoDispute,
        Overflow,
    }
    
    impl fmt::Display for TransactionError {
        fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
            formatter.write_str(match self {
                Self::NegativeAmount => "amount must not be negative",
                Self::DuplicateTransaction => "transaction ID already exists",
                Self::AccountLock => "account lock prevents transactions",
                Self::InsufficientFunds => "insufficient available funds",
                Self::UnknownTransaction => "transaction does not exist",
                Self::ClientMismatch => "transaction belongs to another client",
                Self::WithdrawalControl => {
                    "withdrawal does not support disputes, resolves, or chargebacks"
                }
                Self::DisputeConflict => "transaction has an active dispute or chargeback",
                Self::NoDispute => "transaction requires an active dispute",
                Self::Overflow => "account balance exceeds the numeric range",
            })
        }
    }
    
    impl std::error::Error for TransactionError {}
    
    #[derive(Debug, Default)]
    pub struct Engine {
        clients: HashMap<ClientId, ClientInfo>,
        transactions: HashMap<TxId, TxRecord>,
    }
    
    impl Engine {
        pub fn clients(&self) -> &HashMap<ClientId, ClientInfo> {
            &self.clients
        }
    
        pub fn into_clients(self) -> HashMap<ClientId, ClientInfo> {
            self.clients
        }
    
        pub fn apply(&mut self, transaction: Transaction) -> Result<(), TransactionError> {
            let (amount, deposit) = match transaction.ty {
                TxType::Deposit(amount) => (amount.0, true),
                TxType::Withdrawal(amount) => (amount.0, false),
                _ => return self.apply_control(transaction),
            };
            if amount < 0 {
                return Err(TransactionError::NegativeAmount);
            }
            let entry = match self.transactions.entry(transaction.id) {
                Entry::Vacant(entry) => entry,
                Entry::Occupied(_) => return Err(TransactionError::DuplicateTransaction),
            };
            let account = self
                .clients
                .entry(transaction.client_id)
                .or_insert_with(|| ClientInfo::new(transaction.client_id));
            if account.lock {
                return Err(TransactionError::AccountLock);
            }
            let (total, status) = if deposit {
                (
                    account
                        .total
                        .0
                        .checked_add(amount)
                        .ok_or(TransactionError::Overflow)?,
                    TxStatus::Deposit(Money(amount)),
                )
            } else {
                if account.available().0 < amount {
                    return Err(TransactionError::InsufficientFunds);
                }
                (
                    account
                        .total
                        .0
                        .checked_sub(amount)
                        .ok_or(TransactionError::Overflow)?,
                    TxStatus::Withdrawal,
                )
            };
            account.update(total, account.on_hold.0)?;
            entry.insert(TxRecord {
                client_id: transaction.client_id,
                status,
            });
            Ok(())
        }
    
        fn apply_control(&mut self, transaction: Transaction) -> Result<(), TransactionError> {
            let record = self
                .transactions
                .get_mut(&transaction.id)
                .ok_or(TransactionError::UnknownTransaction)?;
            if record.client_id != transaction.client_id {
                return Err(TransactionError::ClientMismatch);
            }
            let account = self
                .clients
                .get_mut(&transaction.client_id)
                .expect("transaction account missing");
            if account.lock {
                return Err(TransactionError::AccountLock);
            }
            let (total, on_hold, status, lock) = match (transaction.ty, record.status) {
                (TxType::Dispute, TxStatus::Deposit(amount)) => (
                    account.total.0,
                    account
                        .on_hold
                        .0
                        .checked_add(amount.0)
                        .ok_or(TransactionError::Overflow)?,
                    TxStatus::Dispute(amount),
                    false,
                ),
                (TxType::Resolve, TxStatus::Dispute(amount)) => (
                    account.total.0,
                    account
                        .on_hold
                        .0
                        .checked_sub(amount.0)
                        .ok_or(TransactionError::Overflow)?,
                    TxStatus::Deposit(amount),
                    false,
                ),
                (TxType::Chargeback, TxStatus::Dispute(amount)) => (
                    account
                        .total
                        .0
                        .checked_sub(amount.0)
                        .ok_or(TransactionError::Overflow)?,
                    account
                        .on_hold
                        .0
                        .checked_sub(amount.0)
                        .ok_or(TransactionError::Overflow)?,
                    TxStatus::Chargeback,
                    true,
                ),
                (_, TxStatus::Withdrawal) => return Err(TransactionError::WithdrawalControl),
                (TxType::Dispute, _) => return Err(TransactionError::DisputeConflict),
                _ => return Err(TransactionError::NoDispute),
            };
            account.update(total, on_hold)?;
            account.lock = lock;
            record.status = status;
            Ok(())
        }
    }
    
    pub fn process_txs<Input, SourceError, Diagnostics>(
        transactions: Input,
        diagnostics: Diagnostics,
    ) -> anyhow::Result<HashMap<ClientId, ClientInfo>>
    where
        Input: IntoIterator<Item = Result<Transaction, SourceError>>,
        SourceError: Into<anyhow::Error>,
        Diagnostics: Write,
    {
        let mut engine = Engine::default();
        let mut diagnostics = BufWriter::with_capacity(IO_BUFFER_CAPACITY, diagnostics);
        for transaction in transactions {
            let transaction = match transaction {
                Ok(transaction) => transaction,
                Err(error) => {
                    diagnostics.flush().context("failed to write diagnostics")?;
                    let error: anyhow::Error = error.into();
                    return Err(error.context("failed to read transaction"));
                }
            };
            if let Err(error) = engine.apply(transaction) {
                writeln!(
                    diagnostics,
                    "client {}, transaction {}: {error}",
                    *transaction.client_id, *transaction.id
                )
                .context("failed to write diagnostics")?;
            }
        }
        diagnostics.flush().context("failed to write diagnostics")?;
        Ok(engine.into_clients())
    }

    struct RetryReader<Input>(Input);
    
    impl<Input: Read> Read for RetryReader<Input> {
        fn read(&mut self, buffer: &mut [u8]) -> io::Result<usize> {
            loop {
                match self.0.read(buffer) {
                    Err(error) if error.kind() == io::ErrorKind::Interrupted => continue,
                    result => return result,
                }
            }
        }
    }
    
    pub struct CsvTransactions<Input> {
        reader: csv::Reader<RetryReader<Input>>,
        headers: csv::ByteRecord,
        record: csv::ByteRecord,
        stop: bool,
    }
    
    impl<Input: Read> CsvTransactions<Input> {
        pub fn new(input: Input) -> Result<Self> {
            let mut reader = csv::ReaderBuilder::new()
                .trim(csv::Trim::All)
                .buffer_capacity(IO_BUFFER_CAPACITY)
                .from_reader(RetryReader(input));
            let headers = reader.byte_headers().context("failed to read CSV")?.clone();
            let columns: [&[u8]; 4] = [b"type", b"client", b"tx", b"amount"];
            if headers.len() != columns.len()
                || columns
                    .iter()
                    .any(|column| headers.iter().filter(|header| header == column).count() != 1)
            {
                bail!("invalid CSV header: require type,client,tx,amount exactly once in any order");
            }
            Ok(Self {
                reader,
                headers,
                record: csv::ByteRecord::with_capacity(128, 4),
                stop: false,
            })
        }
    
        fn read_transaction(&mut self) -> Result<Option<Transaction>> {
            if !self.reader.read_byte_record(&mut self.record)? {
                return Ok(None);
            }
            let record: CsvTransaction = self.record.deserialize(Some(&self.headers))?;
            let amount = || {
                record.amount.with_context(|| {
                    format!(
                        "missing amount at CSV line {}: deposits and withdrawals require an amount",
                        self.record.position().map_or(0, csv::Position::line)
                    )
                })
            };
            let ty = match record.ty {
                CsvTxType::Deposit => TxType::Deposit(amount()?),
                CsvTxType::Withdrawal => TxType::Withdrawal(amount()?),
                CsvTxType::Dispute => TxType::Dispute,
                CsvTxType::Resolve => TxType::Resolve,
                CsvTxType::Chargeback => TxType::Chargeback,
            };
            Ok(Some(Transaction {
                ty,
                client_id: record.client,
                id: record.tx,
            }))
        }
    }
    
    impl<Input: Read> Iterator for CsvTransactions<Input> {
        type Item = Result<Transaction>;
    
        fn next(&mut self) -> Option<Self::Item> {
            if self.stop {
                return None;
            }
            match self.read_transaction().context("failed to read CSV") {
                Ok(Some(transaction)) => Some(Ok(transaction)),
                Ok(None) => {
                    self.stop = true;
                    None
                }
                Err(error) => {
                    self.stop = true;
                    Some(Err(error))
                }
            }
        }
    }
    
    impl<Input: Read> FusedIterator for CsvTransactions<Input> {}
    
    #[derive(Serialize)]
    struct CsvClient {
        client: ClientId,
        available: Money,
        #[serde(rename = "held")]
        on_hold: Money,
        total: Money,
        #[serde(rename = "locked")]
        lock: bool,

    pub fn write_clients<Output: Write>(
        clients: &HashMap<ClientId, ClientInfo>,
        output: Output,
    ) -> Result<()> {
        let mut writer = csv::WriterBuilder::new()
            .has_headers(false)
            .buffer_capacity(IO_BUFFER_CAPACITY)
            .from_writer(output);
        writer
            .write_record(["client", "available", "held", "total", "locked"])
            .context("failed to write account CSV")?;
        let mut clients: Vec<_> = clients.values().collect();
        clients.sort_unstable_by_key(|client| client.id());
        for client in clients {
            writer
                .serialize(CsvClient {
                    client: client.id(),
                    available: client.available(),
                    on_hold: client.on_hold(),
                    total: client.total(),
                    lock: client.lock(),
                })
                .context("failed to write account CSV")?;
        }
        writer.flush().context("failed to write account CSV")
    }
    
    pub fn process_csv<Input: Read, Output: Write, Diagnostics: Write>(
        input: Input,
        output: Output,
        diagnostics: Diagnostics,
    ) -> Result<()> {
        let transactions = CsvTransactions::new(input)?;
        let clients = process_txs(transactions, diagnostics)?;
        write_clients(&clients, output)
    }

    static NEXT_FILE: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(0);
    
    struct InputFile {
        path: PathBuf,
    }
    
    impl InputFile {
        fn new(input: &str) -> Self {
            let directory = PathBuf::from(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("target/test-inputs");
            std::fs::create_dir_all(&directory).expect("failed to create test directory");
            let sequence = NEXT_FILE.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
            let path = directory.join(format!("{}-{sequence}.csv", std::process::id()));
            std::fs::write(&path, input).expect("failed to create test input");
            Self { path }
        }
    }
    
    impl Drop for InputFile {
        fn drop(&mut self) {
            std::fs::remove_file(&self.path).expect("failed to remove test input");
        }
    }
    
    fn process(input: &str) -> Output {
        let file = InputFile::new(input);
        Command::new(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_legendary-octo-spork"))
            .arg(&file.path)
            .output()
            .expect("failed to execute CLI")
    }
    
    fn balances(input: &str, account_rows: &str, error_count: usize) {
        let output = process(input);
        let diagnostics = String::from_utf8(output.stderr).expect("invalid diagnostic encoding");
        assert!(output.status.success(), "{diagnostics}");
        assert_eq!(
            String::from_utf8(output.stdout).expect("invalid output encoding"),
            format!("client,available,held,total,locked\n{account_rows}")
        );
        assert_eq!(diagnostics.lines().count(), error_count, "{diagnostics}");
    }

    # legendary-octo-spork
    
    Process account transactions from CSV with exact integer arithmetic and four decimal places.
    
    ```sh
    cargo run --release -- input.csv > accounts.csv
    ```
    
    The CLI accepts exactly one file path. It writes account CSV to stdout and transaction errors to stderr. Invalid CSV or an I/O failure produces a nonzero exit status. The processor reads the complete input before it writes account output.
    
    Input requires the columns `type,client,tx,amount` exactly once, in any order. The parser trims surrounding whitespace. Every row must contain four fields; control records can leave `amount` empty.
    
    ```csv
    type,client,tx,amount
    deposit,1,1,2.0001
    withdrawal,1,2,0.5000
    dispute,1,1,
    resolve,1,1,
    deposit,2,3,1
    ```
    
    This input produces:
    
    ```csv
    client,available,held,total,locked
    1,1.5001,0.0000,1.5001,false
    2,1.0000,0.0000,1.0000,false
    ```
    
    Output uses ascending client IDs and exactly four decimal places. Client IDs use `u16`; transaction IDs use `u32`. Both types accept zero. Amount syntax requires integer digits and optionally a decimal point with one to four fractional digits. The processor rejects excess precision, exponent notation, and amounts outside the numeric range. It never rounds or converts amounts through floating point.
    
    | Operation | Requirements | Account changes |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | Deposit | New transaction ID; nonnegative amount | Increase total and available |
    | Withdrawal | New transaction ID; nonnegative amount; sufficient available funds | Decrease total and available |
    | Dispute | The same client's deposit without an active dispute | Increase funds on hold; decrease available |
    | Resolve | The same client's deposit with an active dispute | Decrease funds on hold; increase available |
    | Chargeback | The same client's deposit with an active dispute | Decrease total and funds on hold; lock the account |
    
    A resolve permits another dispute on the same deposit. Withdrawals do not support dispute, resolve, or chargeback. Disputes can make available funds negative after a withdrawal. A chargeback can make total funds negative and prevents all later activity on the account, including changes to other disputes.
    
    Transaction IDs have global scope. The engine rejects duplicate deposits and withdrawals, references to another client's transaction, invalid state changes, negative amounts, and arithmetic overflow. These errors leave balances and transaction status unchanged; the processor reports each error and continues. Only successful deposits and withdrawals reserve new transaction IDs. The first monetary operation with a new transaction ID and a nonnegative amount creates a client account, including a withdrawal with insufficient funds. Invalid control records do not create accounts. Control records always use the deposit amount; a nonempty amount field still requires valid decimal syntax.
    
    The library separates transaction processing from CSV and stream access:
    
    | API | Use |
    | --- | --- |
    | `process_csv(input, output, diagnostics)` | CSV pipeline over any `Read` input and `Write` outputs, using `i64` amounts |
    | `CsvTransactions::new(input)` | Fallible transaction iterator over any `Read` input; reuse one CSV byte record |
    | `process_txs(transactions, diagnostics)` | Consume any iterator of `Result<Transaction, Error>` and return the account map |
    | `Engine::default()` and `apply(transaction)` | Process records incrementally while preserving account and transaction state |
    | `write_clients(&clients, output)` | Serialize an account map to any `Write` output |
    
    Pipeline functions return `anyhow::Result`; transaction source errors must convert into `anyhow::Error`. Error context preserves the operation and source error. Format errors with `{error:#}` to include the complete cause chain. `MoneyError` and `TransactionError` remain separate types.
    
    For memory streams:
    
    ```rust
    use legendary_octo_spork::process_csv;
    
    let input = b"type,client,tx,amount\ndeposit,1,1,1.2345\n";
    let mut output = Vec::new();
    let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
    process_csv(input.as_slice(), &mut output, &mut diagnostics)?;
    ```
    
    For a blocking TCP connection:
    
    ```rust
    use std::net::TcpStream;
    use legendary_octo_spork::process_csv;
    
    fn process_connection(mut stream: TcpStream) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
        let input = stream.try_clone()?;
        process_csv(input, &mut stream, std::io::stderr().lock())
    }
    ```
    
    The peer must finish its input, for example with `shutdown(Shutdown::Write)`, before reading the account response. The integration suite checks this exchange over a real loopback TCP connection. For connections without an end of input, feed records to `Engine::apply` and use `write_clients` when the application requires a snapshot. These APIs use blocking I/O.
    
    `Money(i64)` stores minor units, so `Money(12_345)` represents `1.2345`. Parsing and balance updates use checked `i64` arithmetic. `ClientId`, `TxId`, and `Money` implement `Deref`. Transaction variants require an amount for deposits and withdrawals, and account fields remain private so callers cannot bypass balance checks.
    
    The processor does not collect input records. It reuses CSV record storage and uses 64 KiB buffers for input, output, and diagnostics. The reader retries interrupted reads before CSV parsing. Processing takes expected linear time in the number of records, plus account sorting. Memory grows with client count, unique successful monetary transactions, and the largest CSV record. The engine retains transaction history for duplicate detection, later disputes, and withdrawal validation. Repeated dispute and resolve operations reuse an existing history entry.
    
    Run checks and the throughput benchmark with:
    
    ```sh
    cargo test --locked
    cargo test --release --locked
    cargo fmt --all -- --check
    cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
    cargo bench --bench throughput --locked
    ```
    
    The benchmark generates input before timing, performs one warmup, and reports the median of five runs. Every run checks all account rows and requires an empty diagnostic stream. It covers one million unique deposits and about one million mixed records, including all five transaction types. Adjust its size with `TX_BENCH_ROWS` and its repetitions with `TX_BENCH_ROUNDS`.
    
    On 2026-10-17, Rust 1.94.1 on an Intel Core i9-13900K in this Linux container produced:
    
    | In-memory CSV workload | Records | Median time | Records/second | Input MiB/second |
    | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
    | Unique deposits, 1,024 clients | 1,000,000 | 0.193 s | 5.19 million | 127.65 |
    | Deposits, withdrawals, disputes, resolves, and chargebacks | 1,002,048 | 0.155 s | 6.46 million | 144.50 |
    
    Separate CLI measurements use files with one million and four million rows, with three runs per input and complete output validation. Linux `VmHWM` samples track peak process memory after startup:
    
    | CLI workload | Records | Median time | Records/second | Peak memory |
    | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
    | Unique deposits, 1,024 clients | 1,000,000 | 0.200 s | 4.99 million | 101.3 MiB |
    | Unique deposits, 1,024 clients | 4,000,000 | 0.807 s | 4.96 million | 398.2 MiB |
    | Repeated dispute/resolve on one deposit | 1,000,000 | 0.115 s | 8.73 million | 2.3 MiB |
    | Repeated dispute/resolve on one deposit | 4,000,000 | 0.420 s | 9.53 million | 2.2 MiB |
    
    These measurements describe this environment; the benchmark does not enforce a hardware-dependent timing limit. History growth accounts for the memory increase with unique deposits. Repeated control records do not increase history size.

    pub fn deserialize_string_record<'de, D: Deserialize<'de>>(
        record: &'de StringRecord,
        headers: Option<&'de StringRecord>,
    ) -> Result<D, Error> {
        let mut deser = DeRecordWrap(DeStringRecord {

            headers: headers.map(|r| r.iter()),
            field: 0,
        });
        D::deserialize(&mut deser).map_err(|err| {

    /// An over-engineered internal trait that permits writing a single Serde
    /// deserializer that works on both ByteRecord and StringRecord.
    ///
    /// We *could* implement a single deserializer on `ByteRecord` and simply
    /// convert `StringRecord`s to `ByteRecord`s, but then the implementation
    /// would be required to redo UTF-8 validation checks in certain places.
    ///
    /// How does this work? We create a new `DeRecordWrap` type that wraps
    /// either a `StringRecord` or a `ByteRecord`. We then implement
    /// `DeRecord` for `DeRecordWrap<ByteRecord>` and `DeRecordWrap<StringRecord>`.
    /// Finally, we impl `serde::Deserialize` for `DeRecordWrap<T>` where
    /// `T: DeRecord`. That is, the `DeRecord` type corresponds to the differences
    /// between deserializing into a `ByteRecord` and deserializing into a
    /// `StringRecord`.
    ///
    /// The lifetime `'r` refers to the lifetime of the underlying record.
    trait DeRecord<'r> {
        /// Returns true if and only if this deserialize has access to headers.
        fn has_headers(&self) -> bool;
    
        /// Extracts the next string header value from the underlying record.
        fn next_header(&mut self) -> Result<Option<&'r str>, DeserializeError>;
    
        /// Extracts the next raw byte header value from the underlying record.
        fn next_header_bytes(
            &mut self,
        ) -> Result<Option<&'r [u8]>, DeserializeError>;
    
        /// Extracts the next string field from the underlying record.
        fn next_field(&mut self) -> Result<&'r str, DeserializeError>;
    
        /// Extracts the next raw byte field from the underlying record.
        fn next_field_bytes(&mut self) -> Result<&'r [u8], DeserializeError>;
    
        /// Peeks at the next field from the underlying record.
        fn peek_field(&mut self) -> Option<&'r [u8]>;
    
        /// Returns an error corresponding to the most recently extracted field.
        fn error(&self, kind: DeserializeErrorKind) -> DeserializeError;
    
        /// Infer the type of the next field and deserialize it.
        fn infer_deserialize<'de, V: Visitor<'de>>(
            &mut self,
            visitor: V,
        ) -> Result<V::Value, DeserializeError>;
    }
    
    struct DeRecordWrap<T>(T);
    
    impl<'r, T: DeRecord<'r>> DeRecord<'r> for DeRecordWrap<T> {
        #[inline]
        fn has_headers(&self) -> bool {
            self.0.has_headers()
        }
    
        #[inline]
        fn next_header(&mut self) -> Result<Option<&'r str>, DeserializeError> {
            self.0.next_header()
        }
    
        #[inline]
        fn next_header_bytes(
            &mut self,
        ) -> Result<Option<&'r [u8]>, DeserializeError> {
            self.0.next_header_bytes()
        }
    
        fn deserialize_byte_buf<V: Visitor<'de>>(
            self,
            visitor: V,
        ) -> Result<V::Value, Self::Error> {
            self.next_field_bytes()
                .and_then(|f| visitor.visit_byte_buf(f.to_vec()))
        }
    
        fn deserialize_option<V: Visitor<'de>>(
            self,
            visitor: V,
        ) -> Result<V::Value, Self::Error> {

                Some([]) => {
                    self.next_field().expect("empty field");
                    visitor.visit_none()
                }
                Some(_) => visitor.visit_some(self),
            }
        }
    
        fn deserialize_unit<V: Visitor<'de>>(
            self,
            visitor: V,
        ) -> Result<V::Value, Self::Error> {
            visitor.visit_unit()

            "type,client,tx,amount\nwithdrawal,1,1,\n",

    #[test]
    fn csv_errors_identify_the_row_and_amount_problem() {
        for (input, line, problem) in [
            (
                "type,client,tx,amount\ndeposit,1,1,\n",
                "line 2",
                "missing amount",
            ),
            (
                "type,client,tx,amount\ndeposit,1,1,1\ndeposit,1,2,0.00001\n",
                "line: 3",
                "amount exceeds four decimal places",
            ),
        ] {
            let output = process(input);
            assert!(!output.status.success());
            assert!(output.stdout.is_empty());
            let diagnostics = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr);
            assert!(diagnostics.contains(line), "{diagnostics}");
            assert!(diagnostics.contains(problem), "{diagnostics}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn memory_streams_support_the_csv_pipeline() {
        let input = Cursor::new(b"type,client,tx,amount\ndeposit,1,1,1.2345\n");
        let mut output = Vec::new();
        let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
        process_csv(input, &mut output, &mut diagnostics).expect("failed to process memory input");
        assert_eq!(
            output,
            b"client,available,held,total,locked\n1,1.2345,0.0000,1.2345,false\n"
        );
        assert!(diagnostics.is_empty());
    }
    
    #[test]
    fn transaction_iterators_accept_records_without_csv() {
        let transactions = [
            Transaction {
                client_id: ClientId(7),
                id: TxId(8),
                ty: TxType::Deposit(Money(12_345)),
            },
            Transaction {
                client_id: ClientId(7),
                id: TxId(9),
                ty: TxType::Withdrawal(Money(1)),
            },
        ];
        let clients = process_txs(
            transactions.into_iter().map(Ok::<_, Infallible>),
            io::sink(),
        )
        .expect("failed to process transaction iterator");
        let mut output = Vec::new();
        write_clients(&clients, &mut output).expect("failed to write clients");
        assert_eq!(
            output,
            b"client,available,held,total,locked\n7,1.2344,0.0000,1.2344,false\n"
        );
    }
    
    #[test]
    fn incremental_processing_preserves_state_between_inputs() {
        let mut engine = Engine::default();
        for input in [
            "type,client,tx,amount\ndeposit,1,1,2\n",
            "type,client,tx,amount\ndispute,1,1,\n",
            "type,client,tx,amount\nresolve,1,1,\nwithdrawal,1,2,1\n",
        ] {
            for transaction in
                CsvTransactions::new(input.as_bytes()).expect("failed to create transaction source")
            {
                engine
                    .apply(transaction.expect("failed to read transaction"))
                    .expect("failed to apply transaction");
            }
        }
        assert_eq!(engine.clients()[&ClientId(1)].available(), Money(10_000));
    }
    
    struct ShortStream<Stream> {
        inner: Stream,
        limit: usize,
    }
    
    impl<Stream: Read> Read for ShortStream<Stream> {
        fn read(&mut self, buffer: &mut [u8]) -> io::Result<usize> {
            let length = buffer.len().min(self.limit);
            self.inner.read(&mut buffer[..length])
        }
    }

    README.md:40:A resolve permits another dispute on the same deposit. Withdrawals do not support dispute, resolve, or chargeback. Disputes can make available funds negative after a withdrawal.     README.md:42:Transaction IDs have global scope. The engine rejects duplicate deposits and withdrawals, references to another client's transaction, invalid state changes, negative amounts, and arithmetic overflow. These errors leave balances and transaction status unchanged; the processor reports each error and continues. Only successful deposits and withdrawals reserve new transaction IDs. The first monetary operation with a new transaction ID and a nonnegative amount creates a client account, including a withdrawal with insufficient funds. Invalid control records do not create accounts. Control records always use the deposit amount; a nonempty amount field still requires valid decimal syntax.

    README.md:83:The processor does not collect input records. It reuses CSV record storage and uses 64 KiB buffers for input, output, and diagnostics. Memory grows with client count, unique successful monetary transactions, and the largest CSV record. The engine retains transaction history for duplicate detection, later disputes, and withdrawal validation. Repeated dispute and resolve operations reuse an existing history entry.

    The user requested these changes. The optional Definition of Done approval request is pending.
    
    Known facts:
    - A shared entry operation creates accounts for withdrawals.
    - The history map stores withdrawal markers solely for duplicate detection and a separate error message.

    Assumptions: deposit IDs are unique in valid input. Remove duplicate ID validation. The CSV header still includes amount; control rows can omit a trailing amount field, and any supplied control amount has no effect.

    use std::collections::HashMap;
    use std::fmt;
    use std::io::{BufWriter, Write};
    
    use anyhow::Context;
    
    use crate::{ClientId, IO_BUFFER_CAPACITY, Money, Transaction, TxId, TxType};
    
    #[derive(Clone, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
    pub struct ClientInfo {
        id: ClientId,
        total: Money,
        on_hold: Money,
        lock: bool,
    }
    
    impl ClientInfo {
        fn new(id: ClientId) -> Self {
            Self {
                id,
                total: Money(0),
                on_hold: Money(0),
                lock: false,
            }
        }
    
        pub fn id(&self) -> ClientId {
            self.id
        }
    
        pub fn total(&self) -> Money {
            self.total
        }
    
        pub fn on_hold(&self) -> Money {
            self.on_hold
        }
    
        pub fn available(&self) -> Money {
            Money(
                self.total
                    .0
                    .checked_sub(self.on_hold.0)
                    .expect("account balance overflow"),
            )
        }
    
        pub fn lock(&self) -> bool {
            self.lock
        }
    
        fn update(&mut self, total: i64, on_hold: i64) -> Result<(), TransactionError> {
            total
                .checked_sub(on_hold)
                .ok_or(TransactionError::Overflow)?;
            self.total = Money(total);
            self.on_hold = Money(on_hold);
            Ok(())
        }
    }
    
    #[derive(Debug)]
    struct Deposit {
        client_id: ClientId,
        amount: Money,
        dispute: bool,
    }
    
    #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
    pub enum TransactionError {
        NegativeAmount,
        AccountLock,
        InsufficientFunds,
        UnknownTransaction,
        ClientMismatch,
        DisputeConflict,
        NoDispute,
        Overflow,
    }
    
    impl fmt::Display for TransactionError {
        fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
            formatter.write_str(match self {
                Self::NegativeAmount => "amount must not be negative",
                Self::AccountLock => "account lock prevents transactions",
                Self::InsufficientFunds => "insufficient available funds",
                Self::UnknownTransaction => "transaction does not exist",
                Self::ClientMismatch => "transaction belongs to another client",
                Self::DisputeConflict => "deposit has an active dispute",
                Self::NoDispute => "transaction requires an active dispute",
                Self::Overflow => "account balance exceeds the numeric range",
            })
        }
    }
    
    impl std::error::Error for TransactionError {}
    
    #[derive(Debug, Default)]
    pub struct Engine {
        clients: HashMap<ClientId, ClientInfo>,
        deposits: HashMap<TxId, Deposit>,
    }
    
    impl Engine {
        pub fn clients(&self) -> &HashMap<ClientId, ClientInfo> {
            &self.clients
        }
    
        pub fn into_clients(self) -> HashMap<ClientId, ClientInfo> {
            self.clients
        }
    
        pub fn apply(&mut self, transaction: Transaction) -> Result<(), TransactionError> {
            let (amount, deposit) = match transaction.ty {
                TxType::Deposit(amount) => (amount.0, true),
                TxType::Withdrawal(amount) => (amount.0, false),
                _ => return self.apply_control(transaction),
            };
            if amount < 0 {
                return Err(TransactionError::NegativeAmount);
            }
            let account = if deposit {
                self.clients
                    .entry(transaction.client_id)
                    .or_insert_with(|| ClientInfo::new(transaction.client_id))
            } else {
                self.clients
                    .get_mut(&transaction.client_id)
                    .ok_or(TransactionError::InsufficientFunds)?
            };
            if account.lock {
                return Err(TransactionError::AccountLock);
            }
            let total = if deposit {
                account
                    .total
                    .0
                    .checked_add(amount)
                    .ok_or(TransactionError::Overflow)?
            } else {
                if account.available().0 < amount {
                    return Err(TransactionError::InsufficientFunds);
                }
                account
                    .total
                    .0
                    .checked_sub(amount)
                    .ok_or(TransactionError::Overflow)?
            };
            account.update(total, account.on_hold.0)?;
            if deposit {
                self.deposits.insert(
                    transaction.id,
                    Deposit {
                        client_id: transaction.client_id,
                        amount: Money(amount),
                        dispute: false,
                    },
                );
            }
            Ok(())
        }
    
        fn apply_control(&mut self, transaction: Transaction) -> Result<(), TransactionError> {
            let deposit = self
                .deposits
                .get_mut(&transaction.id)
                .ok_or(TransactionError::UnknownTransaction)?;
            if deposit.client_id != transaction.client_id {
                return Err(TransactionError::ClientMismatch);
            }
            let account = self
                .clients
                .get_mut(&transaction.client_id)
                .expect("transaction account missing");
            if account.lock {
                return Err(TransactionError::AccountLock);
            }
            let amount = deposit.amount.0;
            let (total, on_hold, dispute, lock) = match (transaction.ty, deposit.dispute) {
                (TxType::Dispute, false) => (
                    account.total.0,
                    account
                        .on_hold
                        .0
                        .checked_add(amount)
                        .ok_or(TransactionError::Overflow)?,
                    true,
                    false,
                ),
                (TxType::Resolve, true) => (
                    account.total.0,
                    account
                        .on_hold
                        .0
                        .checked_sub(amount)
                        .ok_or(TransactionError::Overflow)?,
                    false,
                    false,
                ),
                (TxType::Chargeback, true) => (
                    account
                        .total
                        .0
                        .checked_sub(amount)
                        .ok_or(TransactionError::Overflow)?,
                    account
                        .on_hold
                        .0
                        .checked_sub(amount)
                        .ok_or(TransactionError::Overflow)?,
                    false,
                    true,
                ),
                (TxType::Dispute, true) => return Err(TransactionError::DisputeConflict),
                _ => return Err(TransactionError::NoDispute),
            };
            account.update(total, on_hold)?;
            account.lock = lock;
            deposit.dispute = dispute;
            Ok(())
        }
    }
    
    pub fn process_txs<Input, SourceError, Diagnostics>(
        transactions: Input,
        diagnostics: Diagnostics,
    ) -> anyhow::Result<HashMap<ClientId, ClientInfo>>
    where
        Input: IntoIterator<Item = Result<Transaction, SourceError>>,
        SourceError: Into<anyhow::Error>,
        Diagnostics: Write,
    {
        let mut engine = Engine::default();
        let mut diagnostics = BufWriter::with_capacity(IO_BUFFER_CAPACITY, diagnostics);
        Deposit,
        Withdrawal,
        Dispute,
        Resolve,
        Chargeback,
    }
    
    #[derive(Deserialize)]
    struct CsvTransaction<'record> {
        #[serde(rename = "type")]
        ty: CsvTxType,
        client: ClientId,
        tx: TxId,
        #[serde(borrow)]
        amount: Option<&'record str>,
    }
    
    struct RetryReader<Input>(Input);
    
    impl<Input: Read> Read for RetryReader<Input> {
        fn read(&mut self, buffer: &mut [u8]) -> io::Result<usize> {
            loop {
                match self.0.read(buffer) {
                    Err(error) if error.kind() == io::ErrorKind::Interrupted => continue,
                    result => return result,
                }
            }
        }
    }
    
    pub struct CsvTransactions<Input> {
        reader: csv::Reader<RetryReader<Input>>,
        headers: csv::ByteRecord,
        record: csv::ByteRecord,
        stop: bool,
    }
    
    impl<Input: Read> CsvTransactions<Input> {
        pub fn new(input: Input) -> Result<Self> {
            let mut reader = csv::ReaderBuilder::new()
                .trim(csv::Trim::All)
                .flexible(true)
                .buffer_capacity(IO_BUFFER_CAPACITY)
                .from_reader(RetryReader(input));
            let headers = reader.byte_headers().context("failed to read CSV")?.clone();
            let columns: [&[u8]; 4] = [b"type", b"client", b"tx", b"amount"];
            if headers.len() != columns.len()
                || columns
                    .iter()
                    .any(|column| headers.iter().filter(|header| header == column).count() != 1)
            {
                bail!("invalid CSV header: require type,client,tx,amount exactly once in any order");
            }
            Ok(Self {
                reader,
                headers,
                record: csv::ByteRecord::with_capacity(128, 4),
                stop: false,
            })
        }
    
        fn read_transaction(&mut self) -> Result<Option<Transaction>> {
            if !self.reader.read_byte_record(&mut self.record)? {
                return Ok(None);
            }
            if self.record.len() > self.headers.len() {
                bail!(
                    "too many fields at CSV line {}",
                    self.record.position().map_or(0, csv::Position::line)
                );
            }
            let record: CsvTransaction<'_> = self.record.deserialize(Some(&self.headers))?;
            let amount = || {
                let line = self.record.position().map_or(0, csv::Position::line);
                record.amount
                    .with_context(|| format!("missing amount at CSV line {line}: deposits and withdrawals require an amount"))?
                    .parse::<Money>()
                    .with_context(|| format!("invalid amount at CSV line {line}"))
            };
            let ty = match record.ty {
                CsvTxType::Deposit => TxType::Deposit(amount()?),
                CsvTxType::Withdrawal => TxType::Withdrawal(amount()?),
                CsvTxType::Dispute => TxType::Dispute,
                CsvTxType::Resolve => TxType::Resolve,
                CsvTxType::Chargeback => TxType::Chargeback,
            };
            Ok(Some(Transaction {
                ty,
                client_id: record.client,
                id: record.tx,
            }))
        }
    }
    
    impl<Input: Read> Iterator for CsvTransactions<Input> {
        type Item = Result<Transaction>;
    
        fn next(&mut self) -> Option<Self::Item> {
            if self.stop {
                return None;
            }
            match self.read_transaction().context("failed to read CSV") {
                Ok(Some(transaction)) => Some(Ok(transaction)),
                Ok(None) => {
                    self.stop = true;
                    None
                }
                Err(error) => {
                    self.stop = true;
                    Some(Err(error))
                }
    README.md:42:Deposit IDs have global scope, and the processor assumes that input deposit IDs are unique. It performs no duplicate ID validation. Only deposits create accounts. A withdrawal on a missing account returns an error without creating an account. The engine also rejects references to another client's deposit, invalid state changes, negative amounts, and arithmetic overflow. These errors leave balances and deposit state unchanged; the processor reports each error and continues. Disputes, resolves, and chargebacks always use the deposit's full amount.

    $ cat README.md
    # legendary-octo-spork
    
    Process account transactions from CSV with exact integer arithmetic and four decimal places.
    
    ```sh
    cargo run --release -- input.csv > accounts.csv
    ```
    
    The CLI accepts exactly one file path. It writes account CSV to stdout and transaction errors to stderr. Invalid CSV or an I/O failure produces a nonzero exit status. The processor reads the complete input before it writes account output.
    
    Input requires the columns `type,client,tx,amount` exactly once, in any order. The parser trims surrounding whitespace. Deposits and withdrawals require an amount. Dispute, resolve, and chargeback records use only `type`, `client`, and `tx`; they can omit a trailing amount field or leave it empty. Any supplied amount on these records has no effect.
    
    ```csv
    type,client,tx,amount
    deposit,1,1,2.0001
    withdrawal,1,2,0.5000
    dispute,1,1
    resolve,1,1
    deposit,2,3,1
    ```
    
    This input produces:
    
    ```csv
    client,available,held,total,locked
    1,1.5001,0.0000,1.5001,false
    2,1.0000,0.0000,1.0000,false
    ```
    
    Output uses ascending client IDs and exactly four decimal places. Client IDs use `u16`; transaction IDs use `u32`. Both types accept zero. Deposit and withdrawal amounts require integer digits and optionally a decimal point with one to four fractional digits. The processor rejects excess precision, exponent notation, and amounts outside the numeric range. It never rounds or converts amounts through floating point.
    
    | Operation | Requirements | Account changes |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | Deposit | Nonnegative amount | Create the account if necessary; increase total and available |
    | Withdrawal | Existing account; nonnegative amount; sufficient available funds | Decrease total and available |
    | Dispute | The same client's deposit without an active dispute | Increase funds on hold; decrease available |
    | Resolve | The same client's deposit with an active dispute | Decrease funds on hold; increase available |
    | Chargeback | The same client's deposit with an active dispute | Decrease total and funds on hold; lock the account |
    
    A resolve permits another dispute on the same deposit. Withdrawals do not support dispute, resolve, or chargeback. Disputes can make available funds negative after a withdrawal. A chargeback can make total funds negative and prevents all later activity on the account, including changes to other disputes.
    
    Deposit IDs have global scope, and the processor assumes that input deposit IDs are unique. It performs no duplicate ID validation. Only deposits create accounts. A withdrawal on a missing account returns an error without creating an account. The engine also rejects references to another client's deposit, invalid state changes, negative amounts, and arithmetic overflow. These errors leave balances and deposit state unchanged; the processor reports each error and continues. Disputes, resolves, and chargebacks always use the deposit's full amount.
    
    The library separates transaction processing from CSV and stream access:
    
    | API | Use |
    | --- | --- |
    | `process_csv(input, output, diagnostics)` | CSV pipeline over any `Read` input and `Write` outputs, using `i64` amounts |
    | `CsvTransactions::new(input)` | Fallible transaction iterator over any `Read` input; reuse one CSV byte record |
    | `process_txs(transactions, diagnostics)` | Consume any iterator of `Result<Transaction, Error>` and return the account map |
    | `Engine::default()` and `apply(transaction)` | Process records incrementally while preserving account and transaction state |
    | `write_clients(&clients, output)` | Serialize an account map to any `Write` output |
    
    Pipeline functions return `anyhow::Result`; transaction source errors must convert into `anyhow::Error`. Error context preserves the operation and source error. Format errors with `{error:#}` to include the complete cause chain. `MoneyError` and `TransactionError` remain separate types.
    
    For memory streams:
    
    ```rust
    use legendary_octo_spork::process_csv;
    
    let input = b"type,client,tx,amount\ndeposit,1,1,1.2345\n";
    let mut output = Vec::new();
    let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
    process_csv(input.as_slice(), &mut output, &mut diagnostics)?;
    ```
    
    For a blocking TCP connection:
    
    ```rust
    use std::net::TcpStream;
    use legendary_octo_spork::process_csv;
    
    fn process_connection(mut stream: TcpStream) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
        let input = stream.try_clone()?;
        process_csv(input, &mut stream, std::io::stderr().lock())
    }
    ```
    
    The peer must finish its input, for example with `shutdown(Shutdown::Write)`, before reading the account response. The integration suite checks this exchange over a real loopback TCP connection. For connections without an end of input, feed records to `Engine::apply` and use `write_clients` when the application requires a snapshot. These APIs use blocking I/O.
    
    `Money(i64)` stores minor units, so `Money(12_345)` represents `1.2345`. Parsing and balance updates use checked `i64` arithmetic. `ClientId`, `TxId`, and `Money` implement `Deref`. Transaction variants require an amount for deposits and withdrawals, and account fields remain private so callers cannot bypass balance checks.
    
    The processor does not collect input records. It reuses CSV record storage and uses 64 KiB buffers for input, output, and diagnostics. The reader retries interrupted reads before CSV parsing. Processing takes expected linear time in the number of records, plus account sorting. Memory grows with client count, successful deposits, and the largest CSV record. The engine stores deposit amounts, owners, and dispute flags. Withdrawals create no history entries, and repeated dispute and resolve operations update the same deposit.
    
    Run checks and the throughput benchmark with:
    
    ```sh
    cargo test --locked
    cargo test --release --locked
    cargo fmt --all -- --check
    cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
    cargo bench --bench throughput --locked
    ```
    
    The benchmark generates input before timing, performs one warmup, and reports the median of five runs. Every run checks all account rows and requires an empty diagnostic stream. It covers one million unique deposits and about one million mixed records, including all five transaction types. Adjust its size with `TX_BENCH_ROWS` and its repetitions with `TX_BENCH_ROUNDS`.
    
    On 2026-10-17, Rust 1.94.1 on an Intel Core i9-13900K in this Linux container produced:
    
    | In-memory CSV workload | Records | Median time | Records/second | Input MiB/second |
    | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
    | Unique deposits, 1,024 clients | 1,000,000 | 0.193 s | 5.19 million | 127.65 |
    | Deposits, withdrawals, disputes, resolves, and chargebacks | 1,002,048 | 0.155 s | 6.46 million | 144.50 |
    
    Separate CLI measurements use files with one million and four million rows, with three runs per input and complete output validation. Linux `VmHWM` samples track peak process memory after startup:
    
    | CLI workload | Records | Median time | Records/second | Peak memory |
    | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
    | Unique deposits, 1,024 clients | 1,000,000 | 0.200 s | 4.99 million | 101.3 MiB |
    | Unique deposits, 1,024 clients | 4,000,000 | 0.807 s | 4.96 million | 398.2 MiB |
    | Repeated dispute/resolve on one deposit | 1,000,000 | 0.115 s | 8.73 million | 2.3 MiB |
    | Repeated dispute/resolve on one deposit | 4,000,000 | 0.420 s | 9.53 million | 2.2 MiB |
    
    These measurements describe this environment; the benchmark does not enforce a hardware-dependent timing limit. History growth accounts for the memory increase with unique deposits. Repeated control records do not increase history size.
