    use std::error::Error;
    use std::fmt::Write as _;
    use std::time::{Duration, Instant};
    
    use legendary_octo_spork::{Money, process_csv};
    
    const CLIENT_COUNT: u32 = 1024;
    
    struct Workload {
        label: &'static str,
        input: String,
        output: Vec<u8>,
        rows: u64,
    }
    
    fn account_output(counts: &[u32], chargeback: bool) -> Vec<u8> {
        let mut output = String::from("client,available,held,total,locked\n");
        for (client, count) in counts.iter().enumerate() {
            if *count == 0 {
                continue;
            }
            let total = Money(i64::from(*count) * 10_001 - if chargeback { 20_001 } else { 0 });
            writeln!(output, "{client},{total},0.0000,{total},{chargeback}")
                .expect("failed to format benchmark output");
        }
        output.into_bytes()
    }
    
    fn deposits(rows: u32) -> Workload {
        let mut input = String::with_capacity(rows as usize * 32);
        input.push_str("type,client,tx,amount\n");
        let mut counts = vec![0; CLIENT_COUNT as usize];
        for id in 0..rows {
            let client = id % CLIENT_COUNT;
            writeln!(input, "deposit,{client},{id},1.0001").expect("failed to format benchmark input");
            counts[client as usize] += 1;
        }
        Workload {
            label: "deposits",
            input,
            output: account_output(&counts, false),
            rows: u64::from(rows),
        }
    }
    
    fn mixed(groups: u32) -> Workload {
        let mut input = String::with_capacity(groups as usize * 100);
        input.push_str("type,client,tx,amount\n");
        let mut counts = vec![0; CLIENT_COUNT as usize];
        let mut last_ids = vec![0; CLIENT_COUNT as usize];
        for group in 0..groups {
            let client = group % CLIENT_COUNT;
            let id = group * 2;
            writeln!(input, "deposit,{client},{id},2.0001").expect("failed to format benchmark input");
            writeln!(input, "withdrawal,{client},{},1.0000", id + 1)
                .expect("failed to format benchmark input");
            writeln!(input, "dispute,{client},{id}").expect("failed to format benchmark input");
            writeln!(input, "resolve,{client},{id}").expect("failed to format benchmark input");
            counts[client as usize] += 1;
            last_ids[client as usize] = id;
        }
        let mut rows = u64::from(groups) * 4;
        for (client, count) in counts.iter().enumerate() {
            if *count == 0 {
                continue;
            }
            let id = last_ids[client];
            writeln!(input, "dispute,{client},{id}").expect("failed to format benchmark input");
            writeln!(input, "chargeback,{client},{id}").expect("failed to format benchmark input");
            rows += 2;
        }
        Workload {
            label: "mixed",
            input,
            output: account_output(&counts, true),
            rows,
        }
    }
    
    fn execute(workload: &Workload) -> Duration {
        let mut output = Vec::new();
        let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
        let start = Instant::now();
        process_csv(workload.input.as_bytes(), &mut output, &mut diagnostics)
            .expect("failed to process benchmark workload");
        let duration = start.elapsed();
        assert_eq!(output, workload.output, "incorrect benchmark balances");
        assert!(diagnostics.is_empty(), "invalid benchmark transactions");
        duration
    }
    
    fn measure(workload: Workload, rounds: usize) {
        execute(&workload);
        let mut durations: Vec<_> = (0..rounds).map(|_| execute(&workload)).collect();
        durations.sort_unstable();
        let seconds = durations[durations.len() / 2].as_secs_f64();
        println!(
            "{}: rows={} median_seconds={seconds:.6} rows_per_second={:.0} mib_per_second={:.2}",
            workload.label,
            workload.rows,
            workload.rows as f64 / seconds,
            workload.input.len() as f64 / (1024.0 * 1024.0) / seconds
        );
    }
    
    fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> {
        let rows: u32 = std::env::var("TX_BENCH_ROWS")
            .ok()
            .map(|value| value.parse())
            .transpose()?
            .unwrap_or(1_000_000);
        let rounds: usize = std::env::var("TX_BENCH_ROUNDS")
            .ok()
            .map(|value| value.parse())
            .transpose()?
            .unwrap_or(5);
        if rows == 0 || rounds == 0 {
            return Err("benchmark rows and rounds must exceed zero".into());
        }
        measure(deposits(rows), rounds);
        measure(mixed((rows / 4).max(1)), rounds);
        Ok(())
    }
    # legendary-octo-spork
    
    Process account transactions from a CSV file with exact integer arithmetic and four decimal places. The CLI supports file processing; network connections are a possible future use of the library API.
    
    ```sh
    cargo run --release -- input.csv > accounts.csv
    ```
    
    The CLI accepts exactly one file path. It writes account CSV to stdout and transaction errors to stderr. Invalid CSV or an I/O failure produces a nonzero exit status. The processor reads the complete input before it writes account output.
    
    Input requires the columns `type,client,tx,amount` exactly once, in any order. The parser trims surrounding whitespace. Deposits and withdrawals require an amount. Dispute, resolve, and chargeback records use only `type`, `client`, and `tx`; they can omit a trailing amount field or leave it empty. Any supplied amount on these records has no effect.
    
    ```csv
    type,client,tx,amount
    deposit,1,1,2.0001
    withdrawal,1,2,0.5000
    dispute,1,1
    resolve,1,1
    deposit,2,3,1
    ```
    
    This input produces:
    
    ```csv
    client,available,held,total,locked
    1,1.5001,0.0000,1.5001,false
    2,1.0000,0.0000,1.0000,false
    ```
    
    Output uses ascending client IDs and exactly four decimal places. Client IDs use `u16`; transaction IDs use `u32`. Both types accept zero. Deposit and withdrawal amounts require integer digits and optionally a decimal point with one to four fractional digits. The processor rejects excess precision, exponent notation, and amounts outside the numeric range. It never rounds or converts amounts through floating point.
    
    | Operation | Requirements | Account changes |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | Deposit | Nonnegative amount | Create the account if necessary; increase total and available |
    | Withdrawal | Existing account; nonnegative amount; sufficient available funds | Decrease total and available |
    | Dispute | The same client's deposit without an active dispute | Increase funds on hold; decrease available |
    | Resolve | The same client's deposit with an active dispute | Decrease funds on hold; increase available |
    | Chargeback | The same client's deposit with an active dispute | Decrease total and funds on hold; lock the account |
    
    A resolve permits another dispute on the same deposit. Withdrawals do not support dispute, resolve, or chargeback. Disputes can make available funds negative after a withdrawal. A chargeback can make total funds negative and prevents all later activity on the account, including changes to other disputes.
    
    Deposit IDs have global scope, and the processor assumes that input deposit IDs are unique. It performs no duplicate ID validation. Only deposits create accounts. A withdrawal on a missing account returns an error without creating an account. The engine also rejects references to another client's deposit, invalid state changes, negative amounts, and arithmetic overflow. These errors leave balances and deposit state unchanged; the processor reports each error and continues. Disputes, resolves, and chargebacks always use the deposit's full amount.
    
    The library separates transaction processing from CSV and stream access:
    
    | API | Use |
    | --- | --- |
    | `process_csv(input, output, diagnostics)` | CSV pipeline over any `Read` input and `Write` outputs, using `i64` amounts |
    | `Engine::default()` and `apply(transaction)` | Process records incrementally while preserving account and transaction state |
    | `write_clients(&clients, output)` | Serialize an account map to any `Write` output |
    
    Pipeline functions return `anyhow::Result`. Error context preserves the operation and source error. Format errors with `{error:#}` to include the complete cause chain. `MoneyError` and `TransactionError` remain separate types.
    
    For memory streams:
    
    ```rust
    use legendary_octo_spork::process_csv;
    
    let input = b"type,client,tx,amount\ndeposit,1,1,1.2345\n";
    let mut output = Vec::new();
    let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
    process_csv(input.as_slice(), &mut output, &mut diagnostics)?;
    ```
    
    For possible future use with a blocking TCP connection:
    
    ```rust
    use std::net::TcpStream;
    use legendary_octo_spork::process_csv;
    
    fn process_connection(mut stream: TcpStream) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
        let input = stream.try_clone()?;
        process_csv(input, &mut stream, std::io::stderr().lock())
    }
    ```
    
    The peer must finish its input, for example with `shutdown(Shutdown::Write)`, before reading the account response. These APIs use blocking I/O.
    
    `Money(i64)` stores minor units, so `Money(12_345)` represents `1.2345`. Parsing and balance updates use checked `i64` arithmetic. `ClientId`, `TxId`, and `Money` implement `Deref`. Transaction variants require an amount for deposits and withdrawals. Account fields have crate visibility, and the engine validates balance calculations before assigning fields. Client IDs exist as account map keys; output calculates available funds as total minus funds on hold.
    
    The processor does not collect input records. Its CSV loop reuses one byte record and borrows amount text from that record. It uses 64 KiB buffers for input, output, and diagnostics. The reader retries interrupted reads before CSV parsing. Processing takes expected linear time in the number of records, plus account sorting. Memory grows with client count, successful deposits, and the largest CSV record. The engine stores deposit amounts, owners, and dispute flags. Withdrawals create no history entries, and repeated dispute and resolve operations update the same deposit.
    
    Run checks and the throughput benchmark with:
    
    ```sh
    cargo test --locked
    cargo test --release --locked
    cargo fmt --all -- --check
    cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
    cargo bench --bench throughput --locked
    ```
    
    The benchmark generates input before timing, performs one warmup, and reports the median of five runs. Every run checks all account rows and requires an empty diagnostic stream. It covers one million unique deposits and about one million mixed records, including all five transaction types. Adjust its size with `TX_BENCH_ROWS` and its repetitions with `TX_BENCH_ROUNDS`.
    
    On 2026-10-17, Rust 1.94.1 on an Intel Core i9-13900K in this Linux container produced:
    
    | In-memory CSV workload | Records | Median time | Records/second | Input MiB/second |
    | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
    | Unique deposits, 1,024 clients | 1,000,000 | 0.201 s | 4.97 million | 122.20 |
    | Deposits, withdrawals, disputes, resolves, and chargebacks | 1,002,048 | 0.154 s | 6.52 million | 142.73 |
    
    Separate CLI measurements use files with one million and four million rows, with three runs per input and complete output validation. Linux `VmHWM` samples track peak process memory after startup:
    
    | CLI workload | Records | Median time | Records/second | Peak memory |
    | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
    | Unique deposits, 1,024 clients | 1,000,000 | 0.213 s | 4.70 million | 77.4 MiB |
    | Unique deposits, 1,024 clients | 4,000,000 | 0.856 s | 4.67 million | 302.3 MiB |
    | Withdrawals after one initial deposit | 1,000,000 | 0.159 s | 6.28 million | 2.2 MiB |
    | Withdrawals after one initial deposit | 4,000,000 | 0.605 s | 6.61 million | 2.3 MiB |
    | Repeated dispute/resolve on one deposit | 1,000,000 | 0.112 s | 8.92 million | 2.2 MiB |
    | Repeated dispute/resolve on one deposit | 4,000,000 | 0.412 s | 9.70 million | 2.3 MiB |
    
    The withdrawal record counts include the initial deposit. These measurements describe this environment; the benchmark does not enforce a hardware-dependent timing limit. History growth accounts for the memory increase with unique deposits. Withdrawals and repeated control records do not increase history size.

    use std::io::{self, BufWriter, Read, Write};
    
    use anyhow::{Context, Result, bail};
    use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
    
    use crate::{
        ClientId, ClientInfo, Engine, IO_BUFFER_CAPACITY, Money, RECORD_BUFFER_SIZE, RECORD_MAX_FIELDS,
        Transaction, TxId, TxType,
    };
    
    #[derive(Deserialize)]
    #[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
    enum CsvTxType {
        Deposit,
        Withdrawal,
        Dispute,
        Resolve,
        Chargeback,
    }
    
    #[derive(Deserialize)]
    struct CsvTransaction<'record> {
        #[serde(rename = "type")]
        ty: CsvTxType,
        client: ClientId,
        tx: TxId,
        #[serde(borrow)]
        amount: Option<&'record str>,
    }
    
    struct RetryReader<I>(I);
    
    impl<I: Read> Read for RetryReader<I> {
        fn read(&mut self, buffer: &mut [u8]) -> io::Result<usize> {
            loop {
                match self.0.read(buffer) {
                    Err(error) if error.kind() == io::ErrorKind::Interrupted => continue,
                    result => return result,
                }
            }
        }
    }
    
    fn process_txs(
        input: impl Read,
        diagnostics: &mut impl Write,
    ) -> Result<HashMap<ClientId, ClientInfo>> {
        let mut reader = csv::ReaderBuilder::new()
            .trim(csv::Trim::All)
            .flexible(true)
            .buffer_capacity(IO_BUFFER_CAPACITY)
            .from_reader(RetryReader(input));
        let headers = reader.byte_headers().context("failed to read CSV")?.clone();
        let columns: [&[u8]; 4] = [b"type", b"client", b"tx", b"amount"];
        if headers.len() != columns.len()
            || columns
                .iter()
                .any(|column| headers.iter().filter(|header| header == column).count() != 1)
        {
            bail!("invalid CSV header: require type,client,tx,amount exactly once in any order");
        }
        let mut engine = Engine::default();
        let mut record = csv::ByteRecord::with_capacity(RECORD_BUFFER_SIZE, RECORD_MAX_FIELDS);
        while reader
            .read_byte_record(&mut record)
            .context("failed to read CSV")?
        {
            let line = record.position().map_or(0, csv::Position::line);
            if record.len() > headers.len() {
                bail!("too many fields at CSV line {line}");
            }
            let row: CsvTransaction<'_> = record
                .deserialize(Some(&headers))
                .context("failed to read CSV")?;
            let amount = || {
                row.amount
                    .with_context(|| format!("missing amount at CSV line {line}: deposits and withdrawals require an amount"))?
                    .parse::<Money>()
                    .with_context(|| format!("invalid amount at CSV line {line}"))
            };
            let ty = match row.ty {
                CsvTxType::Deposit => TxType::Deposit(amount()?),
                CsvTxType::Withdrawal => TxType::Withdrawal(amount()?),
                CsvTxType::Dispute => TxType::Dispute,
                CsvTxType::Resolve => TxType::Resolve,
                CsvTxType::Chargeback => TxType::Chargeback,
            };
            let transaction = Transaction {
                ty,
                client_id: row.client,
                id: row.tx,
            };
            if let Err(error) = engine.apply(transaction) {
                writeln!(
                    diagnostics,
                    "client {}, transaction {}: {error}",
                    *transaction.client_id, *transaction.id
                )
                .context("failed to write diagnostics")?;
            }
        }
        Ok(engine.into_clients())
    }
    
    #[derive(Serialize)]
    struct CsvClient {
        client: ClientId,
        available: Money,
        #[serde(rename = "held")]
        on_hold: Money,
        total: Money,
        #[serde(rename = "locked")]
        lock: bool,
    }
    
    pub fn write_clients(clients: &HashMap<ClientId, ClientInfo>, output: impl Write) -> Result<()> {
        let mut writer = csv::WriterBuilder::new()
            .has_headers(false)
            .buffer_capacity(IO_BUFFER_CAPACITY)
            .from_writer(output);
        writer
            .write_record(["client", "available", "held", "total", "locked"])
            .context("failed to write account CSV")?;
        for (client_id, client) in clients.iter() {
            writer
                .serialize(CsvClient {
                    client: *client_id,
                    available: Money(client.total.0 - client.on_hold.0),
                    on_hold: client.on_hold,
                    total: client.total,
                    lock: client.lock,
                })
                .context("failed to write account CSV")?;
        }
        writer.flush().context("failed to write account CSV")
    }
    
    pub fn process_csv(input: impl Read, output: impl Write, diagnostics: impl Write) -> Result<()> {
        let mut diagnostics = BufWriter::with_capacity(IO_BUFFER_CAPACITY, diagnostics);
        let clients = process_txs(input, &mut diagnostics);
        diagnostics.flush().context("failed to write diagnostics")?;
        let clients = clients?;
        write_clients(&clients, output)
    }

    #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
    pub enum TransactionError {
        NegativeAmount,
        AccountLock,
        InsufficientFunds,
        UnknownTransaction,
        ClientMismatch,
        DisputeConflict,
        NoDispute,
        Overflow,
    }
    
    impl fmt::Display for TransactionError {
        fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
            formatter.write_str(match self {
                Self::NegativeAmount => "amount must not be negative",
                Self::AccountLock => "account lock prevents transactions",
                Self::InsufficientFunds => "insufficient available funds",
                Self::UnknownTransaction => "transaction does not exist",
                Self::ClientMismatch => "transaction belongs to another client",
                Self::DisputeConflict => "deposit has an active dispute",
                Self::NoDispute => "transaction requires an active dispute",
                Self::Overflow => "account balance exceeds the numeric range",
            })
        }
    }
    
    impl std::error::Error for TransactionError {}
    
    #[derive(Debug, Default)]
    pub struct Engine {
        clients: HashMap<ClientId, ClientInfo>,
        deposits: HashMap<TxId, Deposit>,
    }
    
    impl Engine {
        pub fn clients(&self) -> &HashMap<ClientId, ClientInfo> {
            &self.clients
        }
    
        pub fn into_clients(self) -> HashMap<ClientId, ClientInfo> {
            self.clients
        }
    
        pub fn apply(&mut self, transaction: Transaction) -> Result<(), TransactionError> {
            let (amount, deposit) = match transaction.ty {
                TxType::Deposit(amount) => (amount.0, true),
                TxType::Withdrawal(amount) => (amount.0, false),
                _ => return self.apply_control(transaction),
            };
            if amount < 0 {
                return Err(TransactionError::NegativeAmount);
            }
            let account = if deposit {
                self.clients.entry(transaction.client_id).or_default()
            } else {
                self.clients
                    .get_mut(&transaction.client_id)
                    .ok_or(TransactionError::InsufficientFunds)?
            };
            if account.lock {
                return Err(TransactionError::AccountLock);
            }
            let total = if deposit {
                account
                    .total
                    .0
                    .checked_add(amount)
                    .ok_or(TransactionError::Overflow)?
            } else {
                let available = account
                    .total
                    .0
                    .checked_sub(account.on_hold.0)
                    .ok_or(TransactionError::Overflow)?;
                if available < amount {
                    return Err(TransactionError::InsufficientFunds);
                }
                account
                    .total
                    .0
                    .checked_sub(amount)
                    .ok_or(TransactionError::Overflow)?
            };
            total
                .checked_sub(account.on_hold.0)
                .ok_or(TransactionError::Overflow)?;
            account.total = Money(total);
            if deposit {
                self.deposits.insert(
                    transaction.id,
                    Deposit {
                        client_id: transaction.client_id,
                        amount: Money(amount),
                        dispute: false,
                    },
                );
            }
            Ok(())
        }
    
        fn apply_control(&mut self, transaction: Transaction) -> Result<(), TransactionError> {
            let deposit = self
                .deposits
                .get_mut(&transaction.id)
                .ok_or(TransactionError::UnknownTransaction)?;
            if deposit.client_id != transaction.client_id {
                return Err(TransactionError::ClientMismatch);
            }
            let account = self
                .clients
                .get_mut(&transaction.client_id)
                .expect("transaction account missing");
            if account.lock {
                return Err(TransactionError::AccountLock);
            }
            let amount = deposit.amount.0;
            match (transaction.ty, deposit.dispute) {
                (TxType::Dispute, false) => {
                    let on_hold = account
                        .on_hold
                        .0
                        .checked_add(amount)
                        .ok_or(TransactionError::Overflow)?;
                    account
                        .total
                        .0
                        .checked_sub(on_hold)
                        .ok_or(TransactionError::Overflow)?;
                    account.on_hold = Money(on_hold);
                    deposit.dispute = true;
                }
                (TxType::Resolve, true) => {
                    let on_hold = account
                        .on_hold
                        .0
                        .checked_sub(amount)
                        .ok_or(TransactionError::Overflow)?;
                    account
                        .total
                        .0
                        .checked_sub(on_hold)
                        .ok_or(TransactionError::Overflow)?;
                    account.on_hold = Money(on_hold);
                    deposit.dispute = false;
                }
                (TxType::Chargeback, true) => {
                    let total = account
                        .total
                        .0
                        .checked_sub(amount)
                        .ok_or(TransactionError::Overflow)?;
                    let on_hold = account
                        .on_hold
                        .0
                        .checked_sub(amount)
                        .ok_or(TransactionError::Overflow)?;
                    total
                        .checked_sub(on_hold)
                        .ok_or(TransactionError::Overflow)?;
                    account.total = Money(total);
                    account.on_hold = Money(on_hold);
                    account.lock = true;
                    deposit.dispute = false;
                }
                (TxType::Dispute, true) => return Err(TransactionError::DisputeConflict),
                _ => return Err(TransactionError::NoDispute),
            }
            Ok(())
        }
    }

    #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
    pub enum MoneyError {
        Syntax,
        Precision,
        Overflow,
    }
    
    impl fmt::Display for MoneyError {
        fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
            formatter.write_str(match self {
                Self::Syntax => "amount must contain decimal digits with an optional minus sign",
                Self::Precision => "amount exceeds four decimal places",
                Self::Overflow => "amount exceeds the numeric range",
            })
        }
    }
    
    impl std::error::Error for MoneyError {}
    
    impl FromStr for Money {
        type Err = MoneyError;
    
        fn from_str(text: &str) -> Result<Self, Self::Err> {
            let (negative, digits) = match text.strip_prefix('-') {
                Some(digits) => (true, digits),
                None => (false, text),
            };
            let (whole, fraction) = match digits.split_once('.') {
                Some((whole, fraction)) if !fraction.is_empty() => (whole, fraction),
                Some(_) => return Err(MoneyError::Syntax),
                None => (digits, ""),
            };
            if whole.is_empty() {
                return Err(MoneyError::Syntax);
            }
            if fraction.len() > MONEY_PRECISION as usize {
                return Err(MoneyError::Precision);
            }
            let mut minor_units = 0_i64;
            for digit in whole.bytes().chain(fraction.bytes()) {
                if !digit.is_ascii_digit() {
                    return Err(MoneyError::Syntax);
                }
                let digit_value = i64::from(digit - b'0');
                minor_units = minor_units
                    .checked_mul(10)
                    .and_then(|value| {
                        if negative {
                            value.checked_sub(digit_value)
                        } else {
                            value.checked_add(digit_value)
                        }
                    })
                    .ok_or(MoneyError::Overflow)?;
            }
            for _ in fraction.len()..MONEY_PRECISION as usize {
                minor_units = minor_units.checked_mul(10).ok_or(MoneyError::Overflow)?;
            }
            Ok(Self(minor_units))
        }
    }
    
    impl fmt::Display for Money {
        fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
            let whole = (self.0 / MONEY_SCALE).unsigned_abs();
            let fraction = (self.0 % MONEY_SCALE).unsigned_abs();
            if self.0 < 0 {
                formatter.write_str("-")?;
            }
            write!(
                formatter,
                "{whole}.{fraction:0width$}",
                width = MONEY_PRECISION as usize
            )
        }
    }
    
    impl Serialize for Money {
        fn serialize<Output: Serializer>(
            &self,
            serializer: Output,
        ) -> Result<Output::Ok, Output::Error> {
            serializer.collect_str(self)
        }
    }
    
    struct MoneyVisitor;
    
    impl<'input> Visitor<'input> for MoneyVisitor {
        type Value = Money;
    
        fn expecting(&self, formatter: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
            formatter.write_str("a decimal amount with at most four decimal places")
        }
    
        fn visit_str<Error: de::Error>(self, value: &str) -> Result<Self::Value, Error> {
            value.parse().map_err(de::Error::custom)
        }
    }
    
    impl<'input> Deserialize<'input> for Money {
        fn deserialize<Input: Deserializer<'input>>(deserializer: Input) -> Result<Self, Input::Error> {
            deserializer.deserialize_str(MoneyVisitor)
        }
    }

    use std::path::PathBuf;
    use std::process::{Command, Output};
    use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};
    
    static NEXT_FILE: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(0);
    
    struct InputFile {
        path: PathBuf,
    }
    
    impl InputFile {
        fn new(input: &str) -> Self {
            let directory = PathBuf::from(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("target/test-inputs");
            std::fs::create_dir_all(&directory).expect("failed to create test directory");
            let sequence = NEXT_FILE.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
            let path = directory.join(format!("{}-{sequence}.csv", std::process::id()));
            std::fs::write(&path, input).expect("failed to create test input");
            Self { path }
        }
    }
    
    impl Drop for InputFile {
        fn drop(&mut self) {
            std::fs::remove_file(&self.path).expect("failed to remove test input");
        }
    }
    
    fn process(input: &str) -> Output {
        let file = InputFile::new(input);
        Command::new(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_legendary-octo-spork"))
            .arg(&file.path)
            .output()
            .expect("failed to execute CLI")
    }
    
    fn balances(input: &str, account_rows: &str, error_count: usize) {
        let output = process(input);
        let diagnostics = String::from_utf8(output.stderr).expect("invalid diagnostic encoding");
        assert!(output.status.success(), "{diagnostics}");
        assert_eq!(
            String::from_utf8(output.stdout).expect("invalid output encoding"),
            format!("client,available,held,total,locked\n{account_rows}")
        );
        assert_eq!(diagnostics.lines().count(), error_count, "{diagnostics}");
    }

    impl<Input: Read> Read for InterruptReader<Input> {
        fn read(&mut self, buffer: &mut [u8]) -> io::Result<usize> {
            if self.interrupt {
                self.interrupt = false;
                return Err(io::ErrorKind::Interrupted.into());
            }
            self.interrupt = true;
            let length = buffer.len().min(3);
            self.input.read(&mut buffer[..length])
        }
    }

    #[derive(Serialize)]
    struct CsvClient {
        client: ClientId,
        available: Money,
        #[serde(rename = "held")]
        on_hold: Money,
        total: Money,
        #[serde(rename = "locked")]
        lock: bool,
    }
    
    pub fn write_clients(clients: &HashMap<ClientId, ClientInfo>, output: impl Write) -> Result<()> {
        let mut writer = csv::WriterBuilder::new()
            .has_headers(false)
            .buffer_capacity(IO_BUFFER_CAPACITY)
            .from_writer(output);
        writer
            .write_record(["client", "available", "held", "total", "locked"])
            .context("failed to write account CSV")?;
        for (client_id, client) in clients.iter() {
            writer
                .serialize(CsvClient {
                    client: *client_id,
                    available: Money(client.total.0 - client.on_hold.0),
                    on_hold: client.on_hold,
                    total: client.total,
                    lock: client.lock,
                })
                .context("failed to write account CSV")?;
        }
        writer.flush().context("failed to write account CSV")
    }
    
    pub fn process_csv(input: impl Read, output: impl Write, diagnostics: impl Write) -> Result<()> {
        let mut diagnostics = BufWriter::with_capacity(IO_BUFFER_CAPACITY, diagnostics);
        let clients = process_txs(input, &mut diagnostics);
        diagnostics.flush().context("failed to write diagnostics")?;
        let clients = clients?;
        write_clients(&clients, output)
    }

    import argparse
    import json
    import os
    from pathlib import Path
    import statistics
    import subprocess
    import time
    
    
    def decimal(minor_units):
        magnitude = abs(minor_units)
        sign = "-" if minor_units < 0 else ""
        return f"{sign}{magnitude // 10_000}.{magnitude % 10_000:04}"
    
    
    def create_input(directory, workload, rows):
        path = directory / f"{workload}-{rows}.csv"
        with path.open("w", buffering=1024 * 1024) as stream:
            stream.write("type,client,tx,amount\n")
            if workload == "deposits":
                stream.writelines(f"deposit,{index % 1024},{index},1.0001\n" for index in range(rows))
            elif workload == "withdrawals":
                stream.write(f"deposit,1,0,{decimal(rows - 1)}\n")
                stream.writelines(f"withdrawal,1,{index},0.0001\n" for index in range(1, rows))
            else:
                stream.write("deposit,1,1,1\n")
                stream.writelines(
                    f"{'dispute' if index % 2 == 0 else 'resolve'},1,1\n"
                    for index in range(rows - 1)
                )
        output = "client,available,held,total,locked\n"
        if workload == "deposits":
            for client in range(min(rows, 1024)):
                count = (rows - 1 - client) // 1024 + 1
                total = decimal(count * 10_001)
                output += f"{client},{total},0.0000,{total},false\n"
        elif workload == "withdrawals":
            output += "1,0.0000,0.0000,0.0000,false\n"
        else:
            on_hold = rows % 2 == 0
            output += f"1,{'0.0000,1.0000' if on_hold else '1.0000,0.0000'},1.0000,false\n"
        return path, output.encode()
    
    
    def measure(binary, path, output, rounds):
        output_path = path.with_suffix(".output")
        diagnostic_path = path.with_suffix(".stderr")
        samples = []
        for _ in range(rounds):
            with output_path.open("wb") as stream, diagnostic_path.open("wb") as diagnostics:
                start = time.perf_counter()
                process = subprocess.Popen([str(binary), str(path)], stdout=stream, stderr=diagnostics)
                peak_rss_kib = 0
                status_path = Path(f"/proc/{process.pid}/status")
                while True:
                    child_pid, status, usage = os.wait4(process.pid, os.WNOHANG)
                    if child_pid != 0:
                        break
                    try:
                        for line in status_path.read_text().splitlines():
                            if line.startswith("VmHWM:"):
                                peak_rss_kib = max(peak_rss_kib, int(line.split()[1]))
                    except FileNotFoundError:
                        pass
                    time.sleep(0.001)
                seconds = time.perf_counter() - start
                process.returncode = os.waitstatus_to_exitcode(status)
            if process.returncode != 0:
                raise RuntimeError(diagnostic_path.read_text())
            if diagnostic_path.stat().st_size != 0 or output_path.read_bytes() != output:
                raise RuntimeError("incorrect benchmark output")
            samples.append({
                "seconds": seconds,
                "peak_rss_kib": peak_rss_kib,
                "resource_peak_rss_kib": usage.ru_maxrss,
            })
        return samples
    
    
    def main():
        parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
        parser.add_argument("--rows", nargs="+", type=int, default=[1_000_000, 4_000_000])
        parser.add_argument("--rounds", type=int, default=3)
        arguments = parser.parse_args()
        root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
        directory = root / "target/throughput-inputs"
        directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        binary = root / "target/release/legendary-octo-spork"
        results = []
        for workload in ["deposits", "withdrawals", "disputes"]:
            for rows in arguments.rows:
                path, output = create_input(directory, workload, rows)
                samples = measure(binary, path, output, arguments.rounds)
                seconds = statistics.median(sample["seconds"] for sample in samples)
                result = {
                    "workload": workload,
                    "rows": rows,
                    "input_bytes": path.stat().st_size,
                    "median_seconds": seconds,
                    "rows_per_second": rows / seconds,
                    "peak_rss_kib": max(sample["peak_rss_kib"] for sample in samples),
                    "samples": samples,
                }
                results.append(result)
                print(json.dumps(result), flush=True)
        report = {
            "rustc": subprocess.check_output(["rustc", "--version"], text=True).strip(),
            "results": results,
        }
        (root / ".agent/worklog/throughput.json").write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2) + "\n")
    
    
    if __name__ == "__main__":
        main()

    pub fn assert_accounts(actual: &[u8], expected: &[u8]) {
        let mut actual = csv::Reader::from_reader(actual);

            .trim(csv::Trim::All)

            actual.headers().expect("invalid account output header"),

                .expect("invalid account CSV");
            rows.sort_unstable_by(|left, right| left.iter().cmp(right.iter()));
            rows
        };
        assert_eq!(rows(&mut actual), rows(&mut expected));
    }

        import json
        from pathlib import Path
        import re
        
        literal = r'"(?:\\.|[^"\\])*"'
        balances = re.compile(r'balances\(\s*(' + literal + r')\s*,\s*(' + literal + r')\s*,\s*(\d+)\s*,?\s*\)')
        header = "client,available,held,total,locked\n"
        cli_path = Path("tests/cli.rs")
        cli = cli_path.read_text()
        before = [(json.loads(match[1]), json.loads(match[2]), match[3]) for match in balances.finditer(cli)]
        assert len(before) == 18
        
        def account_header(match):
            expected = json.dumps(header + json.loads(match[2]))
            return f"balances(\n        {match[1]},\n        {expected},\n        {match[3]},\n    )"
        
        cli = balances.sub(account_header, cli)
        cases = re.search(r'for input in \[(.*?)\n    \] \{', cli, re.DOTALL)
        inputs = re.findall(literal, cases[1])
        labels = [
            "empty input",
            "missing amount column",
            "duplicate client column",
            "excess precision after a valid row",
            "empty deposit amount",
            "empty withdrawal amount",
            "missing deposit amount field",
            "missing withdrawal amount field",
            "missing dispute transaction ID",
            "exponent amount",
            "nondecimal amount",
            "amount outside i64 range",
            "client ID outside u16 range",
            "transaction ID outside u32 range",
            "unknown transaction type",
            "extra deposit field",
            "extra dispute field",
        ]
        assert len(inputs) == len(labels)
        entries = "".join(f"        (\n            {json.dumps(label)},\n            {value},\n        ),\n" for label, value in zip(labels, inputs))
        cli = cli[:cases.start()] + "for (case, input) in [\n" + entries + "    ] {" + cli[cases.end():]
        cli = cli.replace('"input: {input}"', '"{case}:\\n{input}"')
        
        def fields(text):
            return tuple(tuple(value.strip() for value in line.split(",")) for line in text.splitlines())
        
        def align(source):
            def replace(match):
                text = json.loads(match[0], strict=False)
                records = fields(text)
                if len(records) < 2 or ("type" not in records[0] and records[0] != tuple(header.strip().split(","))):
                    return match[0]
                widths = [max(len(row[column]) if column < len(row) else 0 for row in records) for column in range(max(map(len, records)))]
                lines = [", ".join(value.ljust(widths[column]) for column, value in enumerate(row)).rstrip() for row in records]
                column = match.start() - source.rfind("\n", 0, match.start())
                result = '"' + ("\n" + " " * column).join(lines)
                if text.endswith("\n"):
                    result += r"\n"
                return result + '"'
            return re.sub(literal, replace, source)
        
        cli = align(cli)
        after = [(json.loads(match[1], strict=False), json.loads(match[2], strict=False), match[3]) for match in balances.finditer(cli)]
        assert len(before) == len(after)
        for previous, current in zip(before, after):
            assert fields(previous[0]) == fields(current[0])
            assert previous[0].endswith("\n") == current[0].endswith("\n")
            assert fields(previous[1]) == fields(current[1])[1:]
            assert current[1].startswith("client")
            assert previous[2] == current[2]
        cli_path.write_text(cli)
        stream_path = Path("tests/streams.rs")
        streams = stream_path.read_text()
        stream_path.write_text(align(streams))
        print(f"converted {len(after)} balance fixtures; account values, input fields, error counts, and final newlines match")
        PY

    mod common;
    
    use std::io::{self, Read, Write};
    
    use common::assert_accounts;
    use legendary_octo_spork::{
        ClientId, Engine, Money, Transaction, TransactionError, TxId, TxType, process_csv,
    };
    
    #[test]
    fn withdrawals_on_missing_accounts_return_errors_without_clients() {
        let mut engine = Engine::default();
        for amount in [0, 10_000] {
            let transaction = Transaction {
                client_id: ClientId(1),
                id: TxId(1),
                ty: TxType::Withdrawal(Money(amount)),
            };
            assert_eq!(
                engine.apply(transaction),
                Err(TransactionError::InsufficientFunds)
            );
            assert!(engine.clients().is_empty());
        }
    }
    
    struct InterruptReader<Input> {
        input: Input,
        interrupt: bool,
    }
    
    impl<Input: Read> Read for InterruptReader<Input> {
        fn read(&mut self, buffer: &mut [u8]) -> io::Result<usize> {
            if self.interrupt {
                self.interrupt = false;
                return Err(io::ErrorKind::Interrupted.into());
            }
            self.interrupt = true;
            let length = buffer.len().min(3);
            self.input.read(&mut buffer[..length])
        }
    }
    
    #[test]
    fn read_interrupts_do_not_discard_partial_transactions() {
        let input = InterruptReader {
            input: b"type   , client, tx, amount
                     deposit, 1     , 1 , 1.0001\n"
                .as_slice(),
            interrupt: true,
        };
        let mut output = Vec::new();
        process_csv(input, &mut output, io::sink()).expect("failed to retry stream interrupts");
        assert_accounts(
            &output,
            b"client, available, held  , total , locked
              1     , 1.0001   , 0.0000, 1.0001, false\n",
        );
    }
    
    struct FaultWriter {
        flush_only: bool,
    }
    
    impl Write for FaultWriter {
        fn write(&mut self, buffer: &[u8]) -> io::Result<usize> {
            if self.flush_only {
                Ok(buffer.len())
            } else {
                Err(io::Error::other("write failure"))
            }
        }
    
        fn flush(&mut self) -> io::Result<()> {
            Err(io::Error::other("flush failure"))
        }
    }
    
    #[test]
    fn output_write_and_flush_errors_do_not_report_success() {
        for flush_only in [false, true] {
            let result = process_csv(
                b"type,client,tx,amount\n".as_slice(),
                FaultWriter { flush_only },
                io::sink(),
            );
            let error = result.expect_err("output failure did not propagate");
            assert!(error.to_string().contains("failed to write account CSV"));
            assert_eq!(
                error.root_cause().to_string(),
                if flush_only {
                    "flush failure"
                } else {
                    "write failure"
                }
            );
        }
    }
    
    #[test]
    fn diagnostic_write_and_flush_errors_do_not_report_success() {
        for input in [
            "type   , client, tx, amount
             dispute, 1     , 1\n",
            "type   , client, tx, amount
             dispute, 1     , 1
             deposit, 1     , 2 , 0.00001\n",
        ] {
            for flush_only in [false, true] {
                let mut output = Vec::new();
                let result = process_csv(input.as_bytes(), &mut output, FaultWriter { flush_only });
                let error = result.expect_err("diagnostic failure did not propagate");
                assert!(error.to_string().contains("failed to write diagnostics"));
                assert_eq!(
                    error.root_cause().to_string(),
                    if flush_only {
                        "flush failure"
                    } else {
                        "write failure"
                    }
                );
                assert!(output.is_empty());
            }
        }
    }
    
    struct FaultReader;
    
    impl Read for FaultReader {
        fn read(&mut self, _: &mut [u8]) -> io::Result<usize> {
            Err(io::Error::other("read failure"))
        }
    }
    
    #[test]
    fn input_failures_do_not_produce_account_output() {
        for input in [
            "",
            "type   , client, tx, amount
                           deposit, 1     , 1 , 1\n",
        ] {
            let mut output = Vec::new();
            let result = process_csv(input.as_bytes().chain(FaultReader), &mut output, io::sink());
            assert!(output.is_empty());
            let error = result.expect_err("input failure did not propagate");
            assert!(error.to_string().contains("failed to read CSV"));
            assert_eq!(error.root_cause().to_string(), "read failure");
        }
    }
    
    #[test]
    fn csv_errors_preserve_prior_diagnostics_and_stop_processing() {
        let input = b"type      , client, tx, amount
                      withdrawal, 1     , 1 , 1
                      deposit   , 1     , 2 , 0.00001
                      withdrawal, 2     , 3 , 1\n";
        let mut output = Vec::new();
        let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
        let error = process_csv(input.as_slice(), &mut output, &mut diagnostics)
            .expect_err("invalid CSV did not stop processing");
        assert!(output.is_empty());
        assert_eq!(
            diagnostics,
            b"client 1, transaction 1: insufficient available funds\n"
        );
        assert_eq!(
            error.root_cause().to_string(),
            "amount exceeds four decimal places"
        );
    }
    pub fn assert_accounts(actual: &[u8], expected: &[u8]) {
        let mut actual = csv::Reader::from_reader(actual);
        let mut expected = csv::ReaderBuilder::new()
            .trim(csv::Trim::All)
            .from_reader(expected);
        assert_eq!(
            actual.headers().expect("invalid account output header"),
            expected.headers().expect("invalid account fixture header")
        );
        let rows = |reader: &mut csv::Reader<&[u8]>| {
            let mut rows = reader
                .records()
                .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()
                .expect("invalid account CSV");
            rows.sort_unstable_by(|left, right| left.iter().cmp(right.iter()));
            rows
        };
        assert_eq!(rows(&mut actual), rows(&mut expected));
    }

    fn process(input: &str) -> Output {
        let file = InputFile::new(input);
        Command::new(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_legendary-octo-spork"))
            .arg(&file.path)
            .output()
            .expect("failed to execute CLI")
    }
    
    fn balances(input: &str, expected_accounts: &str, error_count: usize) {
        let output = process(input);
        let diagnostics = String::from_utf8(output.stderr).expect("invalid diagnostic encoding");
        assert!(output.status.success(), "{diagnostics}");
        assert_accounts(&output.stdout, expected_accounts.as_bytes());
        assert_eq!(diagnostics.lines().count(), error_count, "{diagnostics}");
    }

        import json
        from pathlib import Path
        import re
        
        literal = r'"(?:\\.|[^"\\])*"'
        header = ("client", "available", "held", "total", "locked")
        for path in map(Path, ["tests/cli.rs", "tests/streams.rs"]):
            source = path.read_text()
            def align(match):
                text = json.loads(match[0], strict=False)
                rows = [tuple(value.strip() for value in line.split(",")) for line in text.splitlines()]
                if len(rows) < 2 or ("type" not in rows[0] and rows[0] != header):
                    return match[0]
                widths = [max(len(row[column]) if column < len(row) else 0 for row in rows) for column in range(max(map(len, rows)))]
                lines = [", ".join(value.ljust(widths[column]) for column, value in enumerate(row)).rstrip() for row in rows]
                column = match.start() - source.rfind("\n", 0, match.start())
                return '"' + ("\n" + " " * column).join(lines) + (r"\n" if text.endswith("\n") else "") + '"'
            path.write_text(re.sub(literal, align, source))
        PY

        import json
        from pathlib import Path
        import re
        import subprocess
        
        literal = r'"(?:\\.|[^"\\])*"'
        balance_call = re.compile(r'balances\(\s*(' + literal + r')\s*,\s*(' + literal + r')\s*,\s*(\d+)\s*,?\s*\)')
        account_header = ("client", "available", "held", "total", "locked")
        
        def rows(text):
            return tuple(tuple(field.strip() for field in line.split(",")) for line in text.splitlines())
        
        def fixtures(source, accounts=False):
            result = []
            for match in re.finditer(literal, source):
                text = json.loads(match[0], strict=False)
                records = rows(text)
                if records and ("type" in records[0] or (accounts and records[0] == account_header)):
                    result.append((records, text.endswith("\n")))
            return result
        
        for filename in ["cli.rs", "streams.rs"]:
            before = subprocess.check_output(["git", "show", f"9306a98:tests/{filename}"], text=True)
            after = Path("tests", filename).read_text()
            previous_fixtures = fixtures(before, accounts=filename == "streams.rs")
            current_fixtures = fixtures(after, accounts=filename == "streams.rs")
            assert previous_fixtures == current_fixtures, filename
            if filename == "cli.rs":
                previous_balances = list(balance_call.finditer(before))
                current_balances = list(balance_call.finditer(after))
                assert len(previous_balances) == len(current_balances) == 18
                for previous, current in zip(previous_balances, current_balances):
                    assert rows(json.loads(previous[2], strict=False)) == rows(json.loads(current[2], strict=False))[1:]
                    assert previous[3] == current[3]
            print(f"{filename}: {len(current_fixtures)} CSV fixtures preserve fields, field counts, row order, and final newlines")
        PY

        for amount in [0, 10_000] {
            let transaction = Transaction {
                client_id: ClientId(1),
                id: TxId(1),
                ty: TxType::Withdrawal(Money(amount)),

    struct InterruptReader<Input> {
        input: Input,
        interrupt: bool,
    }
    
    impl<Input: Read> Read for InterruptReader<Input> {
        fn read(&mut self, buffer: &mut [u8]) -> io::Result<usize> {
            if self.interrupt {
                self.interrupt = false;
                return Err(io::ErrorKind::Interrupted.into());
            }
            self.interrupt = true;
            let length = buffer.len().min(3);
            self.input.read(&mut buffer[..length])
        }
    }
    
    #[test]
    fn read_interrupts_do_not_discard_partial_transactions() {
        let input = InterruptReader {
            input: b"type   , client, tx, amount
                     deposit, 1     , 1 , 1.0001\n"
                .as_slice(),
            interrupt: true,
        };
        let mut output = Vec::new();
        process_csv(input, &mut output, io::sink()).expect("failed to retry stream interrupts");
        assert_accounts(
            &output,
            b"client, available, held  , total , locked
              1     , 1.0001   , 0.0000, 1.0001, false\n",
        );
    }

        fn write(&mut self, buffer: &[u8]) -> io::Result<usize> {
            if self.flush_only {
                Ok(buffer.len())
            } else {
                Err(io::Error::other("write failure"))
            }
        }
    
        fn flush(&mut self) -> io::Result<()> {
            Err(io::Error::other("flush failure"))

    }

    pub fn assert_accounts(actual: &[u8], expected: &[u8]) {
        let mut actual = csv::Reader::from_reader(actual);
        let mut expected = csv::ReaderBuilder::new()
            .trim(csv::Trim::All)
            .from_reader(expected);
        assert_eq!(
            actual.headers().expect("invalid account output header"),
            expected.headers().expect("invalid account fixture header")
        );
        let rows = |reader: &mut csv::Reader<&[u8]>| {
            let mut rows = reader
                .records()
                .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()
                .expect("invalid account CSV");
            rows.sort_unstable_by(|left, right| left.iter().cmp(right.iter()));
            rows
        };
        assert_eq!(rows(&mut actual), rows(&mut expected));
    }

    struct RetryReader<I>(I);
    
    impl<I: Read> Read for RetryReader<I> {
        fn read(&mut self, buffer: &mut [u8]) -> io::Result<usize> {
            loop {
                match self.0.read(buffer) {
                    Err(error) if error.kind() == io::ErrorKind::Interrupted => continue,
                    result => return result,
                }
            }
        }
    }
    
    fn process_txs(
        input: impl Read,
        diagnostics: &mut impl Write,
    ) -> Result<HashMap<ClientId, ClientInfo>> {
        let mut reader = csv::ReaderBuilder::new()
            .trim(csv::Trim::All)
            .flexible(true)
            .buffer_capacity(IO_BUFFER_CAPACITY)
            .from_reader(RetryReader(input));
        let headers = reader.byte_headers().context("failed to read CSV")?.clone();
        let columns: [&[u8]; 4] = [b"type", b"client", b"tx", b"amount"];
        if headers.len() != columns.len()
            || columns
                .iter()
                .any(|column| headers.iter().filter(|header| header == column).count() != 1)
        {
            bail!("invalid CSV header: require type,client,tx,amount exactly once in any order");
        }
        let mut engine = Engine::default();
        let mut record = csv::ByteRecord::with_capacity(RECORD_BUFFER_SIZE, RECORD_MAX_FIELDS);
        while reader
            .read_byte_record(&mut record)
            .context("failed to read CSV")?
        {
            let line = record.position().map_or(0, csv::Position::line);
            if record.len() > headers.len() {
                bail!("too many fields at CSV line {line}");
            }
            let row: CsvTransaction<'_> = record
                .deserialize(Some(&headers))
                .context("failed to read CSV")?;
            let amount = || {
                row.amount
                    .with_context(|| format!("missing amount at CSV line {line}: deposits and withdrawals require an amount"))?
                    .parse::<Money>()
                    .with_context(|| format!("invalid amount at CSV line {line}"))
            };
            let ty = match row.ty {
                CsvTxType::Deposit => TxType::Deposit(amount()?),
                CsvTxType::Withdrawal => TxType::Withdrawal(amount()?),
                CsvTxType::Dispute => TxType::Dispute,
                CsvTxType::Resolve => TxType::Resolve,
                CsvTxType::Chargeback => TxType::Chargeback,
            };
            let transaction = Transaction {
                ty,
                client_id: row.client,
                id: row.tx,
            };
            if let Err(error) = engine.apply(transaction) {
                writeln!(
                    diagnostics,
                    "client {}, transaction {}: {error}",
                    *transaction.client_id, *transaction.id
                )
                .context("failed to write diagnostics")?;
            }
        }
        Ok(engine.into_clients())
    }
    
    #[derive(Serialize)]
    struct CsvClient {
        client: ClientId,
        available: Money,
        #[serde(rename = "held")]
        on_hold: Money,
        total: Money,
        #[serde(rename = "locked")]
        lock: bool,
    }
    
    pub fn write_clients(clients: &HashMap<ClientId, ClientInfo>, output: impl Write) -> Result<()> {
        let mut writer = csv::WriterBuilder::new()
            .has_headers(false)
            .buffer_capacity(IO_BUFFER_CAPACITY)
            .from_writer(output);
        writer
            .write_record(["client", "available", "held", "total", "locked"])
            .context("failed to write account CSV")?;
        for (client_id, client) in clients.iter() {
            writer
                .serialize(CsvClient {
                    client: *client_id,
                    available: Money(client.total.0 - client.on_hold.0),
                    on_hold: client.on_hold,
                    total: client.total,
                    lock: client.lock,
                })
                .context("failed to write account CSV")?;
        }
        writer.flush().context("failed to write account CSV")
    }
    
    pub fn process_csv(input: impl Read, output: impl Write, diagnostics: impl Write) -> Result<()> {
        let mut diagnostics = BufWriter::with_capacity(IO_BUFFER_CAPACITY, diagnostics);
        let clients = process_txs(input, &mut diagnostics);
        diagnostics.flush().context("failed to write diagnostics")?;
        let clients = clients?;
        write_clients(&clients, output)
    }

    impl fmt::Display for TransactionError {

                Self::AccountLock => "account lock prevents transactions",

    #[derive(Debug, Default)]
    pub struct Engine {
        clients: HashMap<ClientId, ClientInfo>,
        deposits: HashMap<TxId, Deposit>,
    }
    
    impl Engine {
        pub fn clients(&self) -> &HashMap<ClientId, ClientInfo> {
            &self.clients
        }
    
        pub fn into_clients(self) -> HashMap<ClientId, ClientInfo> {
            self.clients
        }
    
        pub fn apply(&mut self, transaction: Transaction) -> Result<(), TransactionError> {
            let (amount, deposit) = match transaction.ty {
                TxType::Deposit(amount) => (amount.0, true),
                TxType::Withdrawal(amount) => (amount.0, false),
                _ => return self.apply_control(transaction),
            };
            if amount < 0 {
                return Err(TransactionError::NegativeAmount);
            }
            let account = if deposit {
                self.clients.entry(transaction.client_id).or_default()
            } else {
                self.clients
                    .get_mut(&transaction.client_id)
                    .ok_or(TransactionError::InsufficientFunds)?
            };
            if account.lock {
                return Err(TransactionError::AccountLock);
            }
            let total = if deposit {
                account
                    .total
                    .0
                    .checked_add(amount)
                    .ok_or(TransactionError::Overflow)?
            } else {
                let available = account
                    .total
                    .0
                    .checked_sub(account.on_hold.0)
                    .ok_or(TransactionError::Overflow)?;
                if available < amount {
                    return Err(TransactionError::InsufficientFunds);
                }
                account
                    .total
                    .0
                    .checked_sub(amount)
                    .ok_or(TransactionError::Overflow)?
            };
            total
                .checked_sub(account.on_hold.0)
                .ok_or(TransactionError::Overflow)?;
            account.total = Money(total);
            if deposit {
                self.deposits.insert(
                    transaction.id,
                    Deposit {
                        client_id: transaction.client_id,
                        amount: Money(amount),
                        dispute: false,
                    },
                );
            }
            Ok(())
        }
    
        fn apply_control(&mut self, transaction: Transaction) -> Result<(), TransactionError> {
            let deposit = self
                .deposits
                .get_mut(&transaction.id)
                .ok_or(TransactionError::UnknownTransaction)?;
            if deposit.client_id != transaction.client_id {
                return Err(TransactionError::ClientMismatch);
            }
            let account = self
                .clients
                .get_mut(&transaction.client_id)
                .expect("transaction account missing");
            if account.lock {
                return Err(TransactionError::AccountLock);
            }
            let amount = deposit.amount.0;
            match (transaction.ty, deposit.dispute) {
                (TxType::Dispute, false) => {
                    let on_hold = account
                        .on_hold
                        .0
                        .checked_add(amount)
                        .ok_or(TransactionError::Overflow)?;
                    account
                        .total
                        .0
                        .checked_sub(on_hold)
                        .ok_or(TransactionError::Overflow)?;
                    account.on_hold = Money(on_hold);
                    deposit.dispute = true;
                }
                (TxType::Resolve, true) => {
                    let on_hold = account
                        .on_hold
                        .0
                        .checked_sub(amount)
                        .ok_or(TransactionError::Overflow)?;
                    account
                        .total
                        .0
                        .checked_sub(on_hold)
                        .ok_or(TransactionError::Overflow)?;
                    account.on_hold = Money(on_hold);
                    deposit.dispute = false;
                }
                (TxType::Chargeback, true) => {
                    let total = account
                        .total
                        .0
                        .checked_sub(amount)
                        .ok_or(TransactionError::Overflow)?;
                    let on_hold = account
                        .on_hold
                        .0
                        .checked_sub(amount)
                        .ok_or(TransactionError::Overflow)?;
                    total
                        .checked_sub(on_hold)
                        .ok_or(TransactionError::Overflow)?;
                    account.total = Money(total);
                    account.on_hold = Money(on_hold);
                    account.lock = true;
                    deposit.dispute = false;
                }
                (TxType::Dispute, true) => return Err(TransactionError::DisputeConflict),
                _ => return Err(TransactionError::NoDispute),
            }
            Ok(())
        }
    }

        fn from_str(text: &str) -> Result<Self, Self::Err> {

                Some(digits) => (true, digits),
                None => (false, text),
            };
            let (whole, fraction) = match digits.split_once('.') {
                Some((whole, fraction)) if !fraction.is_empty() => (whole, fraction),
                Some(_) => return Err(MoneyError::Syntax),
                None => (digits, ""),
            };
            if whole.is_empty() {
                return Err(MoneyError::Syntax);
            }
            if fraction.len() > MONEY_PRECISION as usize {
                return Err(MoneyError::Precision);
            }
            let mut minor_units = 0_i64;
            for digit in whole.bytes().chain(fraction.bytes()) {
                if !digit.is_ascii_digit() {
                    return Err(MoneyError::Syntax);
                }
                let digit_value = i64::from(digit - b'0');
                minor_units = minor_units
                    .checked_mul(10)
                    .and_then(|value| {
                        if negative {
                            value.checked_sub(digit_value)
                        } else {
                            value.checked_add(digit_value)
                        }
                    })
                    .ok_or(MoneyError::Overflow)?;
            }
            for _ in fraction.len()..MONEY_PRECISION as usize {
                minor_units = minor_units.checked_mul(10).ok_or(MoneyError::Overflow)?;
            }
            Ok(Self(minor_units))
        }
    }
    
    impl fmt::Display for Money {
        fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
            let whole = (self.0 / MONEY_SCALE).unsigned_abs();
            let fraction = (self.0 % MONEY_SCALE).unsigned_abs();
            if self.0 < 0 {
                formatter.write_str("-")?;
            }
            write!(
                formatter,
                "{whole}.{fraction:0width$}",
                width = MONEY_PRECISION as usize
            )
        }
    }
    
    impl Serialize for Money {
        fn serialize<Output: Serializer>(
            &self,
            serializer: Output,
        ) -> Result<Output::Ok, Output::Error> {
            serializer.collect_str(self)
        }
    }
    
    struct MoneyVisitor;
    
    impl<'input> Visitor<'input> for MoneyVisitor {
        type Value = Money;
    
        fn expecting(&self, formatter: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
            formatter.write_str("a decimal amount with at most four decimal places")
        }
    
        fn visit_str<Error: de::Error>(self, value: &str) -> Result<Self::Value, Error> {
            value.parse().map_err(de::Error::custom)
        }
    }
    
    impl<'input> Deserialize<'input> for Money {
        fn deserialize<Input: Deserializer<'input>>(deserializer: Input) -> Result<Self, Input::Error> {
            deserializer.deserialize_str(MoneyVisitor)
        }
    }
